MONITORING MECHANISM OF THE MINISTRY
12.1 Having observed that the achievements of the Ministry in many of the schemes was way off the
targets set and there had been underutilisation of the funds allocated for the schemes, the Committee
desired to know from the Ministry as to what mechanism has been devised by it to monitor and review
the progress of its ongoing schemes/programmes and the details of monitoring/review undertaken during
the last year and the results thereof.
The Ministry informed the Committee as under:-
(i) To ensure proper and effective utilization of funds, the schemes/projects of the Ministry are
being monitored regularly, both at Central level as well as field level.
(ii) Monitoring process, inter alia, includes mandatory audit of accounts of grantee organization,
submission of audited utilization certificates, expenditure statement and a progress report on
the activities conducted by the grantee organization besides field visits by Officers of the
Ministry.
(iii) A mechanism of Nodal Officers has been established, under which each State/UT has been
assigned a senior Officer as its Nodal Officer for regular interaction with them.
(iv) While NRCD has a detailed MIS system for monitoring in place, research projects are monitored/
reviewed by the concerned Expert Review Committees.

15
(v) As part of Pollution Control, Installation of online effluent and emission monitoring in polluting
industry and data connectivity with State Pollution Control Board (SPCB)/CPCB is a step
towards self-monitoring and transparency.
(vi) The Centrally Sponsored Schemes in the Forestry & Wildlife sector have streamlined their
implementation mechanism and release of funds to enable faster disbursement of funds to the
States.
(vii) The Public Finance Management System (PFMS) portal administered by the Controller General
of Accounts, Department of Expenditure and running in the Pay & Accounts Offices under
the Ministry for the past few years was expanded in November, 2015 to include payments in
respect of Non-Plan expenditure. The portal provides for real time reporting of expenditure at
all levels of Program implementation through bank interface, timely MIS and reconciliation of
Government accounts.
(viii) The expanded scope of PFMS will further enable transparency in payments, online monitoring
of expenditure and speedy preparation of Government accounts.  Regular meetings are held
with the Divisional Heads in charge of the Programmes/Schemes to expedite utilization levels.
Instructions have been issued to the Programme Divisions/autonomous bodies/ attached offices
from time to time to improve the pace of utilization.
(ix) The adoption of e-Governance has also aided in good management and regulation of
environmental resources.
12.2 The Committee is of the view that a strong and potent monitoring mechanism is extremely
important for achieving the set objectives and implementation of the schemes.  The Committee
takes note of the monitoring mechanism in place in the Ministry.   However, as brought out in the
preceding paragraphs, the monitoring mechanism failed to ensure proper and effective utilisation
of funds.  Not only the funds allocated have been grossly under-utilised but there has also been a
shortfall in the achievements of the Ministry with respect to the targets set under various schemes,
which also results in delay in the implementation of schemes as well as time and cost over-runs.
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should undertake a review of its
administrative and monitoring mechanism and strengthen the same to ensure that funds allocated
for important schemes/programmes are not underutilised and objectives of the schemes are
achieved.
WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT
13. Like forests, wildlife is also a national resource which not only helps in maintaining the ecological
balance but is also beneficial from economic, recre-ational and aesthetic points of view.  Wildlife management
deals with protecting endangered and threatened species and subspecies and their habitats, as well as the
non-threatened agricultural animals and game species.  The details of the programme under Wildlife
Management are as under:-
(a) Project Tiger
13.1 India launched the holistic “Project Tiger” in 1973 to conserve our critically endangered national
animal - the tiger. Based on the recommendations of the Tiger Task Force, the Wildlife (Protection) Act,
1972 was amended in 2006 for creating the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) to give statutory

16
support for strengthening tiger conservation. The coverage of “Project Tiger” has increased from 9
reserves since inception to 48 tiger reserves spread out in 18 States of the country in 2015.  Though the
focus is on the flagship / umbrella species ‘tiger’ the project strives to maintain the stability of ecosystem
by fostering other tropic levels in the food chain thereby ensuring healthy forests, clean air, clean water
and a clean environment.  NTCA retains oversight through advisories / normative guidelines, based on
appraisal of tiger status, ongoing conservation initiatives and recommendations of specially constituted
Committees.  All India Tiger Estimation, 2014 results shows that India now has 2226 tigers which are
30% increase over the last count and is 70% of the total global tiger population.
(b) Project Elephant
13.2 Project Elephant was launched in 1991-92 as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with following objectives:
(i) To protect elephants, their habitat and corridors;
(ii) To address issues of man-animal conflict; and
(iii) W elfare of domesticated elephant.
13.3 The Committee was informed that financial and technical assistance is being provided to major
elephant bearing States in the country.  Under the scheme, 100% financial assistance is provided to the
concerned State Government for undertaking various activities for scientific management of elephant
habitats.  Presently, the project is being implemented in 22 States / UTs.  There are 29 notified and 3
proposed Elephant Reserves in the country, which are still to be notified by the concerned State
Governments, covering approximately 65,000 sq. km. area.
(c) Strengthening of Wildlife Division
13.4 The scheme was started in 1986 for supporting activities like strengthening of Central Wildlife
Division and Regional Offices and development of infrastructure for better enforcement of Wildlife

Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB), a multi-disciplinary organisation with officials from forests,
police and customs was constituted.  The Regional Offices of Wildlife Preservation were made part of the
Bureau, which is headquartered at Delhi.  The details of physical performance under the scheme during

INTEGRATED DEVELOPMENT OF WILDLIFE HABITATS
13.6 A comprehensive CSS scheme ‘Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats’ was envisaged in
December, 2008 to provide for a broad spectrum of conservation interventions in the field by adding

The modified Scheme has following components: ‘Protection of Wildlife outside Protected Areas’ and

13.7 For supporting wildlife and natural resources lying outside PAs, high-value biodiversity areas outside

activities aimed at conservations of wildlife that inter alia  include habitat improvement practices,
infrastructure development, eco-development, anti-poaching activities, research, training, capacity building,
census of wildlife etc.

15.1 The scheme National Natural Resources Management System (NNRMS) is part of an umbrella

15.2 The Committee was informed that some major projects sponsored under this scheme are as under:-

GENERAL OBSERVATION
16. Pollution prevention is a major global concern because of its harmful effects on people’s
health and the overall environment.  Air Pollution has assumed gigantic proportions in our country.
Growing urbanization, rapid industrialization and increasing population etc. during the last few
years have also tremendously impacted the environmental concerns of the country.  In such a
scenario, the measures taken by Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change for
prevention and control of pollution and maintaining ecological balance have not been
commensurate with the magnitude of the problem.  The budgetary allocations of the Ministry are
considerably low compared to the projections made by the Ministry for the 12th Plan period.
However, the Ministry is not even able to fully utilize the funds which are made available to it and
also falls short of achieving the physical targets set or otherwise.  The Committee is of the view
that the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change needs to be adequately funded for
taking all necessary steps in pursuit of the discharge of its mandate, which includes ensuring
better environment management and preservation of biodiversity including wildlife.  In view of
the foregoing, the Committee recommends that the Ministry, on its part, must prepare a long
term plan, put forth futuristic projections and ensure that the allocated outlays are fully utilized
and targets achieved.

RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS — AT A GLANCE
RATIONALIZATION OF PLAN SCHEMES
The Committee takes note of the rationalisation and merger of some schemes in the budget
allocation of the Department and hopes that the merger of the schemes will provide the required
flexibility to the Ministry for the implementation of the schemes. (Para 2.5)
FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE OF THE DEPARTMENT
The Committee observes that against the approved outlay of  ````` 17,874 crore, the Ministry of
Environment, Forest and Climate Change was allocated only ````` 8459.60 crore during the first four
years of the 12th Plan and the same was reduced to ````` 6893.69 crore at R. E. Stage.  In 2016-17,
allocation of ````` 2000.00 crore  has been made to the Department, raising the actual total allocation
of the Department to ````` 10459.60 crore, which is only 58.51 percent of the allocated approved for
the 12th Five Y ear Plan.  The Ministry was able to spend only 67.33% 74.54% and 74.56% of the
B.E. allocation during 2012-13, 2013-14 and 2014-15 respectively and 84.45% of the B.E. allocation
upto February, 2016 in 2015-16. (Para 3.2)
The Committee is of the view that the very purpose of formulation of schemes/programme
during the Five Year Plans is defeated if adequate financial allocations are not made for them in
time.  It also has an adverse bearing on the execution of these projects.  The Committee is
disappointed to note that instead of being provided the approved allocation, the Ministry has been
provided only 58.51 percent of its approved outlay, thereby adversely affecting the schemes/
programmes of the Ministry in the 12th Five Y ear Plan. (Para 3.4)
The Commi ttee observes that although the actual utilisation of the allocated funds of the
Ministry has been steadily increasing during the last few years, the performance of the
Department in terms of utilisation of funds leaves much to be desired. The Ministry could
utilise only 84.45 percent of the allocation upto February, 2016. Most of the reasons cited by the
Ministry for under-utilisation of funds are administrative and procedural which could have
been avoided.  This also shows lack of planning and foresightedness on part of the Ministry.
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should undertake a review of its
financial performance during the last few years and try to identify the bottlenecks responsible
for not being able to optimally utilise the funds at its disposal so as to improve its performance
on this front in the future. (Para 3.5)
BUDGET ALLOCATION OF THE YEAR 2016-17
The mandate of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change is to ensure
better environment management and preservation of biodiversity including Wildlife.  Although
the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has been allocated 18.1 % more funds
compared to the allocation made in R.E. 2015-16, the Committee is of the view that allocations
are not sufficient for the Ministry to effectively discharge its functions.  In view of the importance
of the task mandated to the Ministry which has all the more relevance in the day-today life of all
of us and our surroundings, the Committee recommends that the budgetary allocation of the
22

23
Ministry should be suitably enhanced at R.E. stage to enable the Ministry to discharge its mandate
effectively. (Para 4.3)
FOREST SURVEY OF INDIA
The Committee notes that although the Forest Survey of India was able to expend nearly
70% of the allocation made upto December, 2015, there is a visible gap in its targets and
achievements in the year 2015-16 in terms of Inventory of Forests (Urban and Research).
Inventory of Forests is one of the major activities of Forest Survey of India and it failed to
achieve its targets in this field.  The Committee recommends that Ministry of Environment,
Forest and Climate Change and Forest Survey of India should seriously consider the matter and
take all necessary measures to ensure that such shortfalls do not recur in future. (Para 6.4)
ZOOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA (ZSI)
The Committee observes that Zoological Survey of India was not able to achieve its targets
in terms of field surveys, Digitisation of National Zoological Specimen, documentation of species
of identified animals, training programme etc. The Zoological Survey of India could also spend
only nearly 64% of the plan allocation during 2015-16 (upto 31.12.2015). The performance of
Zoological Survey of India in terms of both achievements of targets and utilisation of funds,
therefore, is not satisfactory and accordingly, the Committee recommends that the Ministry of
Environment, Forest and Climate Change must take urgent remedial measures to ensure that
the performance of Zoological Survey of India improves on both these fronts and the allocations
made are not underutilised. (Para 7.4)
RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT
The Committee is dismayed to note the big lag between the targets and achievements of the
Ministry in the Research and Development  sector in all parameters during 2014-15 and 2015-16.
The performance in 2015-16 has also been sharp decline compared to the performance in 2014-15.
Facilitating research and development and investing for the same are extremely important for
the development of any nation and for a developing country like India, the critical importance of
Research and Development cannot be overemphasized.  The Committee is of the opinion that
without the desired results, the objective of the Ministry of the Research & Development scheme
cannot be achieved.  The Committee also feels that the existing allocation of the Ministry for
Research & Development is not sufficient and that share of Research & Development from the
plan allocation of the Ministry needs to be increased substantially.  The Committee therefore,
recommends that the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change should pay due attention
towards achieving its targets in Research & Development and adequate budgetary increase should
be made in the allocations of the Ministry at R.E. stage for making additional provisions for
Research & Development. (Para 8.5)
ASSISTANCE FOR ABATEMENT OF POLLUTION
The Committee is of the view that pollution, whether it be air, water or noise, has gone
beyond permissible limits during the last few years and has serious consequences for the health
and well being of the citizens of the country.  However, the Committee finds that the performance
of the Ministry/Central Pollution Control Board in a scheme relating to providing assistance for

24
abatement of pollution in not impressive at all. The Ministry could not achieve the physical
targets r elating to Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations and New Noise Monitoring Stations
while other targets set have been stated to be under process.  Further, the Ministry could utilise
only nearly 35% of the allocation upto December, 2015, which too reflects very poorly on the
performance under this scheme.  At a time when the Ministry is required to address the grave
and critical challenge of deteriorating air and water quality and increasing noise pollution, the
Ministry has not been able to fully utilise the allocations made for a scheme providing assistance
for abatement of pollution.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should
take a serious note of its performance under this scheme and take all necessary measures to
ensure that the targets under the scheme are achieved in future and funds allocated are optimally
utilised. (Para 9.4)
NATIONAL ACTION PLAN ON CLIMATE CHANGE
The Committee is dismayed to note that the Ministry had utilised only 14.53 crore for the
programme in 2015-16 (upto 31st December, 2015) out of the allocated B.E. sum of ````` 136.79 crore,
which is only 11% of the funds allocated the year 2015-16.  The Committee had in its 254th
Report also highlighted the gross underutilisation of funds under this scheme during the years
2012-13, 2013-14 and 2014-15.  The performance of the Ministry in 2015-16 has been no better.
The Committee is at a loss to understand as to how a Ministry which is not even able to make use
of a fraction of the funds made available for Climate Change Action Programme, would undertake
additional interventions in the requisite areas of the Programme. A glance at the allocations
made and expenditure incurred under the programme during the last few years indicates that the
Ministry does not require huge funds for the programme.  The Committee, therefore, recommends
that the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change should make a realistic assessment
of the funds required for the programme and seek allocations accordingly so that the allocations
made are not underutilized in successive years. (Para 10.5)
BIOSPHERE RESERVES
The Committee notes that the Ministry was able to utilise only around 50% of its annual
allocation upto December, 2015, which shows a very casual approach of the Ministry towards in-
situ conservation of representative ecosystems of major bio-geographic zones of the country having
global importance.  The Committee recommends that the Ministry should undertake a review of
the schedule of activities under the scheme and plan its activities in a manner that there is no
underutilisation of funds. (Para 11.5)
MONITORING MECHANISM OF THE MINISTRY
The Committee is of the view that a strong and potent monitoring mechanism is extremely
important for achieving the set objectives and implementation of the schemes.  The Committee
takes note of the monitoring mechanism in place in the Ministry.   However, as brought out in the
preceding paragraphs, the monitoring mechanism failed to ensure proper and effective utilisation
of funds.  Not only the funds allocated have been grossly under-utilised but there has also been a
shortfall in the achievements of the Ministry with respect to the targets set under various schemes,
which also results in delay in the implementation of schemes as well as time and cost over-runs.
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should undertake a review of its

25

achieved. (Para 12.2)

Management.  As regards Project Elephant, the Committee recommends that the Ministry should,

As regards Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats, the Committee is constrained to
note that financial assistance could not be provided to important wildlife habitats which exist

REPORT
INTRODUCTION
Understanding and study of the Earth System and its Components and processes is important for
the mankind. The Earth, being a single, interlinked and self-regulating system, together with its components
i.e. atmosphere, oceans, cryosphere, geosphere and biosphere exhibit complex interactions. The scientific
understanding of the Earth system becomes necessary for the improvement of the services for socio-
environment benefits of the country. The exploration of polar regions, sea bed and optimum use of
resources and greater accuracy in the forecast of weather, climate is significant for the sustenance of
life on earth.
1.2 The Ministry of Earth Sciences was established in 2006 by the Government of India for better
understanding of the complex processes of the Earth system namely ocean, atmosphere, cryosphere and
solid work. To monitor and give an overall policy direction of the Ministry, the Earth System Science
Organisation (ESSO) was also established in the year 2007.
1.3 The Ministry is mandated to provide weather and climate services in varied sectors of agriculture,
aviation, shipping, natural disasters (cyclones, earthquakes, tsunamis), marine resources, coastal and
marine ecosystem, climate change and under water technology. The Ministry also deals with Antarctica/
Arctic and Seismological research in an integrated manner.
OBJECTIVES AND FUNCTIONS OF THE MINISTRY
2.1 The Ministry of Earth Sciences has the following objectives and functions:
• Improving weather forecast and provide advisory to agriculture, aviation, shipping, sports
including the Extended Long Range Seasonal Monsoon forecast;
• Providing a wide range of ocean information advisories including fishery information;
• Improving the understanding of Polar Science and its implications for climate change;
• Developing technology for harnessing marine resources;
• Conducting survey for assessing non-living resources;
• Assessing coastal marine productivity and Marine Ecosystems;
• Improving understanding of Climate Change Science;
• Providing early warning of natural hazards viz. cyclone, tsunami, sea level rise; and
• Promoting basic research including capacity building in the Earth Systems Science.
ORGANISATIONAL STRUCTURE OF THE MINISTRY
3.1 The Ministry of Earth Sciences functions through the Earth Commission. The executive arm of the
Ministry i.e. 'The Earth System Science Organisation (ESSO)' is responsible for implementing its policies

2
and programmes. It has four major branches of earth sciences viz., (i) Ocean Science and Technology
Services; (ii) Atmospheric and Climate Science Services; (iii) Geoscience and Technology; and (iv) Polar
Science and Cryosphere. The policies/programmes of the ESSO are being pursued through its autonomous
bodies and subordinate offices. The institutions under the ESSO include India Meteorological Department
(IMD), National Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasting (NCMRWF) and Indian Institute of
Tropical Meteorology (IITM), National Centre for Antarctica and Ocean Research (NCAOR), National
Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS),
Centre for Marine Living Resources & Ecology (CMLRE) and Integrated Coastal and Marine Area
Management (ICMAM).
3.2 The detailed budget allocation of the Ministry of Earth sciences, for the year 2016-17 was considered
by the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science & Technology, Environment &
Forests in its meeting held on the 29th March, 2016.

POLAR SCIENCES AND CRYOSPHERE
6.1 The programme of Polar Sciences and Cryosphere entails the study of Antarctica, Arctic and
glaciers of Himalayas and the impact of climate change in these polar regions and variability in polar
environment has a large global impact. The Ministry had informed that the main objective of Polar and
Cryosphere studies is to carry out an integrated study on glaciology, biogeochemical processes and ice-
core records to understand the role and response of cryosphere in polar/glacial regions and their global
linkages. The Committee desired to know the details and studies/activities about the programme. The
Ministry informed that in Antarctica, scientific studies focuses on Atmospheric and Ocean Sciences,
Earth Sciences and Glaciology, Biological and Environmental-Sciences, Engineering and Communication
and Human Physiology & Medicine. In Arctic, the thrust areas of the research have been atomospheric
sciences with special emphasis on the study of aerosols and precipitation; cryosphere studies on the mass
balance of glaciers and chemical characterization of snow; and biogeochemical studies in Kongsfjorden
(with respect to long-term monitoring of climate change studies). Under the Himalayan Cryosphere
Studies, six major glaciers (Samudra Tapu, Bara Shigri, Sutri Dhaka, Batal, Gepang Gath, and Kunzum)
of Chandra Basin in Lahaul-Spiti region with different characteristics and dynamics are being studied for
their long-term mass balance, energy balance and hydrological balance characteristics. A field Station
with facilities for accommodation and labs is under establishment.
6.2 The Ministry further informed that India attained 'Observer' status within the Arctic council for
conducting scientific research. The Third Antarctic Station "Bharati" was successfully commissioned in
March, 2012 for operations towards conducting front line research and a satellite ground receiving
station has been set up at the Bharati Station in the Antarctica for acquiring data from all passing polar
orbiting satellites. Also, Arctic mooring Observation system has been established. Towards augmentation

5
of ocean observations networks, the retrieval of Arctic Observatory and deployment of Polar Remotely
Operable Vehicle (PROVe) in the Antarctic were carried in July, 2015 and February, 2015, respectively.
6.3 The Committee observed that the budgetary allocation to the programme of Polar Sciences and
Cryosphere in 2015-16 was ` 294.00 crore at B.E. stage which was reduced to ` 123.50 crore at
R.E. stage. The Committee desired to know the reasons for the reduction in funds. In response, the
Ministry, informed that the primary reason for reduction of ` 123.50 crore at RE stage is due to technical
reasons relating to finalization of tender for exhibition of Polar Research Vessel. The L-1 bidder identified
through the tendering process had sought change in terms and conditions of the contract which were
not acceptable resulting into re-tendering and reduction in the expenditure.
6.4 The Committee desired to know why no amount has been allocated to this programme in the
budgetary allocation in 2016-17. The Ministry apprised the Committee that the expenditure for this
programme would be met from the rationalization scheme of PACER for which an amount of ` 156.00
crore has been earmarked during 2016-17.
6.5 The Committee feels that the programme is extremely significant from the environmental,
aspect as it is through this programme that India's presence in Arctic and Antarctica region will
be felt. Further, the study of climate of Polar regions will help in its research of understanding
the climate of cold and fragile region of Himalayas in the wake of climate change. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the Ministry should undertake more studies and activities in the
Polar regions and should take up this programme sincerely.
6.6 The Committee further recommends that the Ministry should undertake a realistic
assessment of all the formalities involved in the programme and take action accordingly so that
underutilization of funds is avoided. The Committee notes that the budgetary allocation to the
new rationalized programme, 'PACER' has been reduced in 2016-17 and hopes that the reduction
would not affect the targets of the programme.
SEISOMOLGICAL AND GEOSCIENCE (SAGE) PROGRAMME

related studies on seismology and earthquakes; research related to solid-earth and geosciences related
drilling programmes in Koyna Warna region (Maharashtra), crustal processes and other related studies/
research activities.
7.2 The Committee desired to know from the Ministry about the main activities proposed to be taken
up in the coming years. The Ministry informed that following programmes are to be undertaken:-
(i) Drilling and instrumentation of pilot bore hole (s) in Koyna towards finalization of main
borehole.
(ii) Construction of Borehole Geophysical Research Laboratory at Karad (Maharashtra) as an
operational centre for carrying out the research activities related to the scientific deep drilling,
borehole investigations, core analysis and research, and associated fields/ research studies
(iii) augmentation of seismological network (iv) initiate construction activities related to National
Centre for Seismology (NCS) (v) provide VSAT connectivity to stand alone BBS & GPS
systems (vi) set up facility for Geochronology.

Seismology causing underutilization of funds which could have been avoided and the progress of

7.7 The Ministry informed that the scientific deep drilling programme in Koyna -Warna region of
Maharashtra is being implemented by Ministry in close association with National Geophysical Research
Institute (NGRI) as per the Cabinet approval.
7.8 As part of the 'Preparatory Phase', various studies/investigations were taken up which included
Broadband Seismology, Magneto-Tellurics (MT), Land-based Gravity-Magnetics, Airborne Gravity and
LIDAR surveys, etc. These studies were supplemented by the exploratory boreholes at a depth of 1.5
km surrounding the seismic zone. Out of the 10 planned boreholes, 9 have been completed to depths
of 1522.5m (Rasati), 1196m (Udgiri), 1134m (Kundi), 1211.6m (Nayari), 906.0M (Phansavle), 1500m
(Panchgani), 1503m (Ukhalu), 1500m (Paneri), 1103m (Khadi) with logging and heat flow measurements.
7.9 The Committee desired to know the status of the main phase of the SAGE programme. In response,
the Ministry informed the Committee that in the main phase, it planned to drill and instrument the pilot

7
borehole (s) (~3 km deep) at identified locations in the Koyna-Warna region in the next one and half years
to be followed by detailed design and drilling of the deep borehole(s) of 5-7 km each. The Ministry
informed that in addition, core samples are being analysed to take various studies, including petrological,
mineralogical, geochemical, paleomagnetic, rock magnetic, anisotropy of magnetic susceptibility etc. and
have been shared for multi-disciplinary investigations (national participation).
7.10 The Committee desired to know whether the Ministry is planning to undertake scientific deep
drilling programme in other parts/regions of India facing regular occurrence of earthquakes apart from
Koyna-Warna region of Maharashtra. The Ministry informed that no such proposal exists currently for
undertaking a scientific deep drilling programme in other parts of India.
7.11 The Committee notes that the activities in the main phase have been initiated by the
Ministry and hopes that the drilling process would be started. The Committee recommends that
the Ministry should complete the drilling process within the scheduled time period to enrich its
prediction of the regular occurrence of the earthquake in the region. The Committee also
recommends to undertake scientific drilling programme in other parts of India facing regular
occurrence of earthquakes.
NATIONAL CENTRE FOR SEISMOLOGY
8.1 The Committee desired to know about the status of National Centre for Seismology and the
progress achieved with regard to creation of manpower, posts, infrastructure etc. The Ministry informed
that National Centre for Seismology (NCS) has been set up as an Attached Office of the Ministry of Earth
Sciences vide Administrative Order No. MoES/25/15/2012-Estt. dated 20.8.2014. A committee was set
up to work out details of separation of manpower, posts, infrastructure, equipment, etc. from the India
Meteorological Department (IMD) to NCS. The proposal for creation of manpower is under process. The
necessary land for construction of NCS building has been identified in IMD campus at Ayanagar in New
Delhi.
8.2 In its previous reports (Report Nos. 243 and 260), the Committee had recommended for
early creation of manpower, posts, infrastructure etc. for National Centre for Seismology. The
Committee, however, notes that even after a period of more than four years, the Ministry is still
in process of creation of manpower. Although the land for the construction of building has been
identified, the construction of the building is yet to be taken up. The Committee finds that the
approach of the Ministry in the matter is extremely lethargic. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the Ministry should initiate the process of construction of the building of
National Centre for Seismology without any further delay.

POLYMETALLIC NODULES AND GAS HYDRATES
11.1 Polymetallic Nodules found at the sea bottom at a depth of 4km to 5km in the Central Indian Ocean
Basin are of essential elements like copper, nickel, cobalt and manganese which are important for future
resources and also the strategic economic reasons.

10
11.2 On being asked about the progress achieved on polymetallic nodule programme, the Ministry
informed the Committee that the survey exploration and environmental impact assessment studies have
been carried out. The data pertaining to various environmental parameters including biological, chemical
and physical oceanographic aspects have been collected. Feasibility of the studies has been carried out
for phase-wise development of the deep sea mining system. Further, the data collected during the earlier
cruises pertaining to survey and exploration were processed for refinement of identification of test mine
site and in addition various research and development endeavour have been carried out pertaining to the
extractive metallurgy of polymetallic nodules and the data collected during the earlier cruises were
processed and analysed. The Ministry further informed that the Cabinet Note for signing the 15 years
contract with the International Seabed Authority for Exploration of Polymetallic Sulphides in the South
West Indian Ridge has been prepared and is being circulated to the various Ministries.
11.3 The Committee desired to know the activities/laboratory experiments conducted by the Ministry for
exploring gas-hydrates and the results of these activities and experiments. The Ministry informed that
under the science component of the Gas Hydrate Programmes various locations have been identified in
Krishna, Godavari and Mahanadi Basins based on the seismic survey and under the technology component,
the autonomous coring system has been developed which can operate upto a depth of 3000 mtrs with
a coring capability of upto 100 mtrs. Further the Remotely Operated Submersible (ROSUB) has been
developed as an exploring tool for the gas hydrates.
11.4 The Ministry also informed that presently no technology is available to the Ministry for exploration
of gas from gas hydrates. However, in this regard pilot lab experiment is being carried out by National
Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT).
11.5 The Committee takes note of the progress made in harnessing polymetallic nodules and the
explorations being carried out by the Ministry which is significant for economic and strategic
purpose. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should continue with the
exploration and also to develop the deep sea mining system. The Committee also notes the
experiment being carried out for feasibility of extracting gas from gas hydrates and recommends
that the Ministry should continue with experiments in this field.
11.6 On acquiring of dedicated research vessels for exploration of poly metallic sulphides, the Committee
asked the Ministry about the progress made in this regard. The Ministry informed that a detailed project
report for acquisition of new vessels will be prepared by consultant appointed following the tender
process. Further, Ministry has tied up with GSI through a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) for
carrying out topographic survey of the Exclusive Economic Zone through deployment of the research
vessel, Samudra Ratnakar.
11.7 The Committee observes that not much progress has been made by the Ministry in acquiring
new dedicated research vessels for the exploration. The Committee also notes that only one
research vessel i.e. Samudra Ratnakar has been deployed. The Committee therefore, recommends
that the Ministry should prudently undertake the acquiring of new vessel and these vessel(s)
should be deployed, without which the exploration of poly metallic sulphides is not feasible.

of the Indian monsoon rainfall for 2016 using the IITM-CFS coupled model, Sub-seasonal forecasting
(2-3 weeks in advance) of the active and break monsoon cycles during 2016, Sub-seasonal forecasting
experiments during non-monsoon season ( i.e, April-June temperatures heat wave conditions and post-
monsoon weather phenomena) are also to be taken up and conduct climate change simulation experiments

13
using the IITM Earth System Model (IITM ESM), Regional Data Assimilation with radar observations
at 4-km resolution will be undertaken under Climate Change Research.
12.5 The Committee notes the increase in allocation at R.E. stage in 2015-16 and in B.E.
2016-17 and exhorts the Ministry to achieves its targets and undertake the schemes/programmes
essential for studying monsoon and climate change and for forecasting experiments.
HIGH PERFORMANCE COMPUTING (HPC)
13.1 The Development of High Performance Computing is significant for improving the quality of
atmospheric, oceanic, polar and geosciences services and enhancing accuracy in monsoon forecasts,
studies related to observation simulation experiments (OSE) and targeted observation experiments, ensemble
predictions for weather, ocean state, cyclone track, short and medium range weather forecast, satellite
and in-situ data assimilation, understanding of the science of climate change and climate variability, etc.
13.2 The Ministry informed the Committee that in order to process and assimilate huge volume of global
scale, weather and climate data for a suite of forecast models, computation facilities have been substantially
augmented to the Petaflop scale.
13.3 The Committee enquired about the reasons for drastic reduction in the amount in the financial year
2015-16 from ` 10.00 crore at B.E. to ` 0.50 crore at the R.E. stage. The Ministry stated that the
allocation of ` 10.00 for the year 2015-16 was for operation and maintenance which was maintained
from the available resources at respective centres of the Ministry. The Ministry also informed that no
separate budgetary allocation has been made during 2016-17 as the necessary budget required to meet
HPC programme has been projected under the ACROSS scheme as a part of rationalization exercise.
13.4 The Committee desired to know about the progress made in High Performance Computing. The
Ministry informed that the HPC has been augmented to ½ peta flop capacity which is fully utilized and
the ultimate goal of acquiring the 10 peta flop capability is being implemented in phased manner and the
purpose is to completely utilize it and cater to the needs of various programmes of the Ministry.
13.5 The Ministry also informed the Committee that its target in the XIIth Five year Plan is to upscale
the High Performance Computing to 4-5 petaflops during the current year 2016-17 for implementing
advanced suite of forecast models for improved forecast quality. However the Ministry is not able to
proceed due to non-availability of funds.
13.6 The Committee in its meeting on 29th March, 2016 stressed upon the need of High Powered
Computers and for high level of computing without which a country stands nowhere. The Committee
also observed that it had underlined the importance of high powered computers since the year 2014.
13.7 The Committee notes that on the one hand, the available BE of ````` 10 crore for the programme
in 2015-16 was reduced to ````` 0.50 crore at RE stage and on the other hand the Ministry is not
able to upscale the High Performance Computing due to non-availability of funds. The Committee
is of the view that replies given by the Ministry are contradictory and recommends that the
Ministry should first utilise the funds available at its disposal and then complain about the lack
of funds. The Committee also recommends that sincere efforts be made for achieving augmentation
of High Performance Computing to the level of 10 Peta flop in time bound manner.

14
ACCURACY IN WEATHER FORECASTING
14.1 The Ministry is responsible for making weather forecasting for the country as a whole and region-
wise also. The Ministry informed the Committee that the weather forecasting capacities have been
enhanced after the implementation of improved forecast suits of models on commissioning of High
Performance computing (HPC) systems. Assimilation of all global radiance data (including INSAT 3D
data) has enhanced the weather forecasting capacities for the production of forecast products at 22 km
grid globally and 9kms/3kms grid over India/regional/mega city domains.
14.2 The Ministry informed that efforts are continuously made to optimize the level of efficiency of the
forecasting systems, with accurate prediction of Very Severe Cyclonic Storms "Phailin", "Hudhud" and
the heavy rainfall events during monsoon seasons of the years 2013 and 2014. However, to improve it
further, the Ministry has been continuously striving for upgradation of (i) observation systems,
(ii) advanced data assimilation tools, (iii) advanced communication and IT infrastructure (iv) high
performance computing systems and (v) intensive/sophisticated training of the personnel to facilitate the
implementation of advanced global/regional/ meso-scale prediction models for improving the accuracy of
weather forecasts in all temporal and spatial scales and for quick dissemination of weather forecast
assessments/warnings to the users.
14.3 The Ministry further informed that success has been achieved in improving the heavy rainfall
warnings. During the XII th Plan, under the National Monsoon Mission initiative, other institutions of
ESSO, the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (ESSO-IITM), Pune, Indian National Centre for
Ocean Information Services (ESSO-INCOIS), Hyderabad and National Centre for Medium Range Weather
Forecasting (ESSO/NCMRWF), NOIDA have embarked upon to build a state-of-the-art coupled ocean-
atmospheric weather & climate model for: (a) improved prediction of monsoon rainfall on extended range
to seasonal time scale (16 days to one season); and (b) improved prediction of temperature, rainfall and
extreme weather events on short to medium range time scale (up to 15 days) so that forecast skill gets
quantitatively improved further for operational services of ESSO-IMD.
14.4 The Committee desired to know about steps taken by the Ministry to bring the accuracy of weather
forecasts at par with the international standards. The Ministry informed that ESSO-IMD is a member
of the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) which is a specialised agency of United Nations
wherein collaborative mechanism with international organisations like U K Meteorological Office (UKMO),
National Centre for Environmental prediction (NCEP), USA etc. exists for exchange of operational
forecasts. Through Indo-US collaboration, a "Monsoon Desk" has been set up jointly for improving
seasonal forecast of the Indian monsoon rainfall through exchanging their ideas and sharing their expertise.
This effort has led to appreciable improvements in the efficiency of models in making better forecasts.
14.5 The Committee takes note of the efforts being made by the Ministry to improve its efficiency
in weather forecasting which is essential in the wake of climate change and unpredictable
weather phenomena. The Committee, however, feels that much more still needs to be done to
improve the accuracy and to bring it at par with international standards. The Committee therefore
recommends that the Ministry should improve its weather forecasting capacities and the upscaling
of High Performance Computing and should also go for collaboration with other nations having
well equipped and advanced weather forecasting systems.

15
WATER DESALINATION PLANTS
15.1 The Committee had visited the water desalination plant established by National Institute of Ocean
Technology (NIOT), Chennai, Ministry of Earth Sciences at Agatti, Lakshadweep in November, 2015 and
January, 2016. The Committee was informed that MoES-NIOT established the first LTTD plant in
Kavaratti during July, 2005 and after the initial maintenance and training for about one year, handed over
the plant to UT administration in 2006. Based on the functioning of the plant, Administration approached
MoES-NIOT to put up plants in other islands of the region. Desalination plants at Minicoy (April, 2011)
and Agatti (July 2011) have been completed in phase 1 and were handed over to the UT Administration
during August and October, 2012. All the three plants are being maintained by the Public Works Department
of UT Administration using the local manpower, to fulfill the needs of the 10,000 strong local community
in each of these plants. The salinity of the fresh water produced at the plants was reduced from 35000
ppm for the seawater to about 180 ppm whereas the permissible limit for drinking water is 2000 ppm.
It was also informed that subsequent to the commencement of the plant water supply for drinking water
needs, have been significantly drop in the incidence of water borne diseases amongst the local people.
The Committee desired to know whether similar water desalination plants were also being established in
other islands of Lakshadweep to cater to the drinking water needs of the people residing there and if
so, what was the status of the projects.
15.2 The Ministry of Earth Sciences intimated that recognizing the Ministry's capability on development,
demonstration and establishment of desalination plants, the Lakshadweep Administration had requested
for setting up of water desalination plants in six more islands viz., Amini, Chetlet, Kadamat, Kalpeni,
Kiltan and Androth. ESSO-NIOT had submitted a detailed project report (DPR) to the Ministry of
Drinking Water and Sanitation (MoDWS) during June, 2013, through Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)
and Union Territory of Lakshadweep Administration (UTL). The proposal was reviewed by the Ministry
of Drinking Water and Sanitation through a standing committee under the chairmanship of JS (Water),
MoDWS. A Central Committee constituted by the Standing Committee reviewed the Techno-commercial
feasibility of the project and recommended the project at a cost of ` 280.01 Crore. The Union Territory
of Lakshadweep submitted documents to MoDWS. The SFC memo as sought by MoDWS was submitted
by NIOT on 30th December, 2015 to Union Territory of Lakshadweep / Ministry of Home Affairs. The
Union Territory of Lakshadweep has also submitted the documents to MoDWS. The Ministry also
informed the Committee that the project is likely to be completed in 48 months from the date of
administrative approval.
15.3 The Committee commends the establishment of water desalination plants by MoES-NIOT in
Kavaratti, Minicoy and Agatti islands of UT of Lakshadweep, constructed with indigenous
components by using limited infrastructure available in these remote islands. These plants are
greatly catering to the need of fresh quality drinking water in these remote islands and are
extremely cost effective. However, the projects for similar plants at other six islands i.e. Amini,
Chetlet, Kadamat, Kalpeni, Kiltan and Androth, which were conceptualised in the year 2013, are
still hanging fire and mired in administrative procedures. Keeping in view the need for fresh
water in these remote islands for human consumption, the Committee recommends that the
Ministry should coordinate with all the concerned Ministries so that all procedural formalities for
the establishment of the water desalination plants at the six islands are completed at the earliest
and the work on the projects begins without any further delay.

AGRO-METEOROLOGICAL SERVICES
16.1 The Committee desired to know the measures being taken by the Ministry to enhance the dissemination
of agro-advisories to farmers and in increasing the agro-met services. The Ministry informed that at
present, 11.5 million farmers are directly receiving the messages under Gramin Krishi Mausam Seva
(GKMS) in vernacular languages. Block level forecast for 37 districts (342 blocks) has been initiated on
pilot mode. The Ministry in association with Agro Met Field Units (AMFUs) is disseminating agro-
meteorological advisories to the farmers through different multichannel system television and visual media
communication through Newspaper and Internet, SMS and IVRS In addition, agro-meteorological advisories
are also disseminated through Kisan Portal launched by the Ministry of Agriculture.
16.2 ESSO-IMD is taking continuous efforts to expand popularization of the service among the farming
community and for this Farmers Awareness Programmes are being conducted in various parts of the
country. Besides these, details of more number of farmers are collected through Kisan Portal and along
with the experts from Agromet Field Units (AMFUs) located at State Agricultural Universities, institutes
of Indian Council of Agriculture Research (ICAR) and Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) participate
in Kisan Melas, Farmers' Day etc. to create awareness about the services so that more farmers get
benefitted.
16.3 The Ministry in the meeting held on 29th March, 2016 informed the Committee that at present 30%
of farmers are being benefitted from the agromet advisories issued twice in a week and the Ministry
wanted to improve it to 80% or 90%. On this, the Committee had advised the Ministry to undertake
measures to ensure awareness and publicity among farmers for such advisories.
16.4 The Committee observes that the number of farmers receiving agro-meteorological advisories
is still small as compared to the total number of farmers in the country. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that efforts should be made in increasing the number of farmers benefiting
from meteorological advisories and enhancing dissemination through various media channels.
The Committee feels that awareness about the agro-met services is necessary and recommends
to continue creating awareness so that more and more farmers get benefited.

of the programme of the Ministry. The Ministry informed that at present, there are 3 training schools
established at ESSO-IITM, Pune, ESSO-INCOIS, Hyderabad and ESSO-IMD, New delhi for the
development of manpower. Also, focused Research and Development is being conducted. The Ministry
informed that with respect to Earth Systems Sciences and Climate, three batches of trainees have already
been imparted the 18 month induction programme. The Ministry also informed that the International
Student Hostel to be jointly shared by MoES-IMD and MoES-IITM for the activities of two training
schools is under construction which will be completed by the end of this financial year i.e. 2016-17.
17.2 The details of the Budget Allocation and Utilization of the programme Research Education, Training
and outreach are as follow:-

ENVIRONMENT MONITORING AND RESEARCH
18.1 The SAF AR-Air was launched on 17th February 2015 to provide site specific information on Air
Quality in near real time and its forecast for the next 24 hours for Delhi, Pune and Mumbai. The SAFAR-
Air monitoring and prediction is being done with the network of monitoring stations in and around
national capital Delhi and Pune on environmental degradation on weather and vice-versa. The Ministry
stated that the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and
Climate Change monitors various pollutants in major towns and cities in the country in association with
State Pollution Control Boards. On the other hand, Ministry of Earth sciences had embarked upon

18
providing air quality forecasts of selected pollutants at selected locations of Delhi (24 hours in advance)
based on measurement network established in close vicinity of the various venues of Commonwealth
Games events that was organised by India in 2010.
18.2 The Committee enquired about what is being done in order to bridge the substantial research gaps
existing in environment related matters by coordinated interaction of scientists of SAFAR and Central
Pollution Control Board. The Ministry informed that the data quality is controlled and the project SAFAR
is ISO 9001-2008 accredited and recognized by World Meteorological Organisation (GURME Programme)
that establishes the credibility and the veracity of data. The frequency of status update is hourly. SAFAR
system involves 4 major components (i) Establishing Air Quality and Weather Monitoring Network
(2) Customizing air quality and weather forecasting model (3) Emission inventory development for the
city (4) Disseminating air quality and weather information products in terms of Air Quality Index (AQI),
through Digital Display boards, SAFAR web portal (safar.tropmet.res.in) and IVRS.
18.3 The Committee observes that not much has been done by the Ministry to bridge the
substantial research gaps between SAFAR and CPCB. The Committee feels that the coordination
between different Ministries is important and therefore recommends to ensure coordination
among concerned Institutions and Ministries which would boost studies and research specially in
environment-related research and development. The Committee also feels that inter-Ministry
coordination is essential without which the benefits of any research activity will not be able to
reach the citizens and to contribute to socio-economic development of the country.

RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS — AT A GLANCE
FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE OF THE MINISTRY AND BUDGETARY ALLOCATIONS FOR
2016-17
The Committee notes that although there has been a reduction in the budgetary allocation
at RE stage in 2015-16, the Ministry has not been able to utilize the allocated amount optimally
and much amount had remained unspent. The Committee, therefore, recommends that such
underutilization by the Ministry should be avoided and whatever amount is allocated should be
utilized to the fullest extent. (Para 4.2)
The Committee notes that the Ministry still requires additional funds in the 'Plan' component
in order to pursue important programmes and activities in 2016-17 which had been deferred
previously due to paucity of funds. The Committee also notes that the 'Plan' component in any
budgetary allocation is important to carry out programmes and activities. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the additional funds for the flagship programmes of the Ministry should be
allocated to the Ministry. The Committee also recommends that the Ministry should be provided
adequate additional amount, as requested by the Ministry, so that the critical programmes are
not adversely affected. (Para 4.6)
POLAR SCIENCES AND CRYOSPHERE
The Committee feels that the programme is extremely significant from the environmental,
aspect as it is through this programme that India's presence in Arctic and Antarctica region will
be felt. Further, the study of climate of Polar regions will help in its research of understanding
the climate of cold and fragile region of Himalayas in the wake of climate change. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the Ministry should undertake more studies and activities in the
Polar regions and should take up this programme sincerely. (Para 6.5)
The Committee further recommends that the Ministry should undertake a realistic
assessment of all the formalities involved in the programme and take action accordingly so that
underutilization of funds is avoided. The Committee notes that the budgetary allocation to the
new rationalized programme, 'PACER' has been reduced in 2016-17 and hopes that the reduction
would not affect the targets of the programme. (Para 6.6)
SEISMOLOGICAL AND GEOSCIENCE (SAGE) PROGRAMME
The Committee notes that the funds were underutilized in 2015-16 primarily due to
postponement of construction of building of National Centre for Seismology. The Committee
feels that the Ministry should not have postponed the construction of National Centre for
Seismology causing underutilization of funds which could have been avoided and the progress of
projects would not have been affected. (Para 7.6)
The Committee notes that the activities in the main phase have been initiated by the
Ministry and hopes that the drilling process would be started. The Committee recommends that
the Ministry should complete the drilling process within the scheduled time period to enrich its
prediction of the regular occurrence of the earthquake in the region. The Committee also

recommends to undertake scientific drilling programme in other parts of India facing regular
occurrence of earthquakes. (Para 7.11)
NATIONAL CENTRE FOR SEISMOLOGY
In its previous reports (Report Nos. 243 and 260), the Committee had recommended for
early creation of manpower, posts, infrastructure etc. for National Centre for Seismology. The
Committee, however, notes that even after a period of more than four years, the Ministry is still
in process of creation of manpower. Although the land for the construction of building has been
identified, the construction of the building is yet to be taken up. The Committee finds that the
approach of the Ministry in the matter is extremely lethargic. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the Ministry should initiate the process of construction of the building of
National Centre for Seismology without any further delay. (Para 8.2)
MICROZONATION OF CITIES
The Committee observes that the Microzonation of cities falling in seismic zone of V , IV and

vulnerability of India to severe earthquakes. (Para 9.2)

The Committee notes the initiatives planned to be taken by the Ministry in 2016-17 and the
amount of expenditure incurred in 2015-16. The Committee hopes that the Ministry would
diligently and prudently work towards these initiatives. The Committee also notes that the
Ministry has failed to acquire Ocean Research Vesssels in last four years which is significant for
conducting oceanic research despite the Committee's repeated recommendations in its previous
reports (Report Nos. 243 and Report No. 260). The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
Ministry should make all out efforts to ensure that such vessels are acquired at the earliest.
(Para 10.4)
POLYMETALLIC NODULES AND GAS HYDRATES
The Committee takes note of the progress made in harnessing polymetallic nodules and the
explorations being carried out by the Ministry which is significant for economic and strategic
purpose. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should continue with the
exploration and also to develop the deep sea mining system. The Committee also notes the
experiment being carried out for feasibility of extracting gas from gas hydrates and recommends
that the Ministry should continue with experiments in this field. (Para 11.5)
The Committee observes that not much progress has been made by the Ministry in acquiring
new dedicated research vessels for the exploration. The Committee also notes that only one
research vessel i.e. Samudra Ratnakar has been deployed. The Committee therefore, recommends
that the Ministry should prudently undertake the acquiring of new vessel and these vessel(s)
should be deployed, without which the exploration of poly metallic sulphides is not feasible.

within 60 to 80 seconds before occurrence of an earthquake.
21. The Committee desired to know about the work done by the Ministry in the agricultural sector. The
Committee was informed that the Ministry was issuing agriculture forecasting and agromet advisories on
weather, rainfall etc. Further, advice was being given by the scientists to the farmers on sowing, use
of fertilizers etc. The Committee advised the Ministry to have a mobile application for farmers and to
increase the number of farmers receiving agromet advisories. The Committee also emphasized the need
for increasing publicity with regard to the services provided by the Ministry.
22. Thereafter, the Members of the Committee raised queries on various subjects such as offshore
numerical tanks; modernisation of systems for early warning of natural hazards like cyclones, floods,
tsunamis, etc. in the wake of increased frequency of natural disasters in the country; steps taken to
tackle the problems of fog, cyclones, tornadoes etc.; establishment of water desalination plants in the
country, including solar desalination units; deep sea technology; marine pollution caused by drilling deep

with other concerned Ministries/Departments etc.
23. The representatives of the Ministry replied to some of the queries raised by the Chairman and

some experts on the subject. The Committee also undertook a study visit to Bengaluru and Goa from
4th to 7th February, 2016 and discussed the subject with the representatives of Union Ministry of
Environment, Forest and Climate Change and Tobacco Board at its meeting held at Bengaluru on 4th
February, 2016.
3. The Committee expresses its thanks to the Officers of the Ministries of Environment, Forest and
