REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Science and
Technology on the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred and Ninety-sixth Report of the
Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology, Environment and
Forests on the Demands for Grants (2017-18) of the Department of Science and Technology, presented
to both the Houses of Parliament on 31st March, 2017. There were 29 recommendations/observations
in the Two Hundred and Ninety-sixth Report of the Committee. Action Taken notes on the recommendations
of the Committee were received from the Department on 4th August, 2017.
The Committee's recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee on the
Action Taken by the Department of Science and Technology are set out in the following paragraphs:–
TWELFTH FIVE YEAR PLAN OUTLAY AND ITS UTILISATION
Recommendation
The Committee notes that during the financial year 2016-17, total plan BE allocation of 
` 4000.00
crore was slightly reduced to ` 3981.00 crore at RE stage whereas Non-Plan allocation of ` 496.32 crore
was increased to ` 512.83 crore at RE stage. However, the Department has been able to utilise only

completion of financial year, the Committee is afraid that the Department will not be able to fully utilise

Recommendation

under some schemes particularly in Supercomputing Mission and Survey of India. The Committee

merged; it would be ensured that the amounts allocated for activities under erstwhile Plan schemes do
not remain unutilized.

highest level, the Department will meet the targets in respect of the above two programmes.

NATIONAL SUPERCOMPUTING FACILITY AND CAPACITY BUILDING MISSION
Recommendation
The Committee finds that in total ` 2740 cr. were earmarked for Supercomputing in Twelfth Five
Year Plan. However the Programme has not taken off till date. Under the programme, total actual
utilisation from 2012-13 to 2016-17 has been only 
` 82.64 cr. against total B.E. allocation of ` 2740.00
cr. in five years. In 2016-17 total allocation was ` 120.00 cr . which was reduced to ` 90.00 cr . at R.E.
but actual utilisation of funds by 31st January, 2017 was only ` 76 lakhs. The financial performance
of the Programme during the last five years makes it clear that the performance of the Programme has
been extremely poor. (Para 16.8)
Action Taken
The National Supercomputing Facility and Capacity Building Mission was approved by the Cabinet
on 25.03.2015 with the administrative approval issued by D/o Electronics and Information Technology
(DeitY) on 09.04.2015. The expenditure under the project started only from financial year 2015-16 after
the approval of the Cabinet. The expenditure against RE allocation has been close to 97.5% in the first
year of implementation 2015-16 and about 99.92% in 2016-17.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply.
Recommendation
The Committee observes that there has been undue delay in the operationalisation of National
Supercomputing Programme. The inordinate delay in holding of meeting of National Empowerment
Board is inexplicable as it resulted in undue delay in the operationalisation of Mission, practically ruling
out the possibility of making any significant headway for realising the Mission. (Para 16.11)
The Committee, therefore, expresses its strong displeasure that the Department has not even been
able to fully utilise funds meant for operationalisation of Supercomputing Mission and recommends that
the Department should ensure full utilisation of allocated resources and should ask for additional funds
only when it is in a position to utilise additional funds asked for by it. The Committee is also of the
considered view that the procedural aspects of the National Supercomputing Mission could have been
handled in a better way and a proactive approach should have been adopted to get the desired result
which sadly is lacking. (Para 16.12)
The Committee also finds that India was a leader in Supercomputing till 2005 but it has now slipped
down in the global ranking. The Committee is of the view that boosting indigenous efforts in
Supercomputing capability is in strategic interests of India, more so when Information Technology
capabilities of the country are recognised worldwide. The Committee recommends that considering the

13
significance of Supercomputing, the Department should make every possible effort to execute the programme
in a mission mode, with a view to avoid any delay. (Para 16.13)
Action Taken
In the 2nd year of its implementation, the Expert Groups in all four verticals namely Infrastructure,
Research and Development, Applications Development and Human Resources were constituted in April,
2016, under the guidance of NSM-Technical Advisory Committee (NSM-TAC). Subsequently, the Expert
Groups met together first in April, 2016 and then had independent meetings.
Based on the Expert Group on Infrastructure recommendations and subsequent discussions in the
NSM-TAC, the NSM-TAC reviewed and approved the Mission Implementation Strategy Document and
Preliminary Design Review (PDR) document for the various specifications/ capacities of supercomputers.
Subsequently, in the 2nd meeting of NSM-Executive Board (NSM-EB) in December, 2016, based on the
recommendations of NSM-TAC, it approved providing 6 supercomputers with data centres (3 in build
mode and 3 in buy mode) to 6 Institutions by the end of 2017. The Institutions have been informed and
visited by the teams of IISc and CDAC who have guided them in making the infrastructure ready for
installation of supercomputers.
The NSM-EB also approved development of Applications in few areas in Phase 1 which include the
following:
(i) Drug Development Platform
(ii) Predictive and Personalized Medicine
(iii) Materials and Computational Chemistry
(iv) Climate, Weather and Disaster Prediction
(v) Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) for Engineering Applications
(vi) Digital Agriculture
Based on the approval of the EB, short-term and medium-term courses on High Performance
Computation (HPC) System Administration have been started by C-DAC at IIT-Mumbai.
The expenditure during the financial year 2016-17 was 99.92% against RE.
The Department is making every effort in executing the NSM along with Ministry of Electronics
and Information Technology.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the action taken. The Committee, however, would like to be
apprised of the progress achieved on a regular basis.

qualitative parameters in terms of utilization of resources of the National Mission on Nano Science and
Technology and set regulatory framework for Nano Science and Technology expeditiously.
(Para 17.12)
Action Taken
Nano Mission has utilized 98.93% of enhance Revised Estimates of ` 125 crore during the FY
2016-17. An allocation of ` 136 crore is made in the Budget Estimates for 2017-18. Nano Mission
Secretariat already has a set of qualitative parameters while assessing the proposals received under the
Mission. It also has a monitoring mechanism embedded in the process for qualitative monitoring of the
sanctioned proposal midterm during the period of implementation. However, the guidance provided by
Parliamentary Standing Committee is accepted by the Mission.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply and would like to be apprised of the details of
qualitative parameters in terms of utilisation of resources of the National Mission on Nano
Science and Technology during Demands for Grants 2018-19.
EFFORTS FOR RETAINING RESEARCH TALENT IN THE COUNTRY
Recommendation
The Committee takes note of the schemes run by the Department that have resulted in arresting brain
drain of accomplished scientists to India particularly Visiting Advanced Joint Research Scheme and
Overseas Visiting Doctoral Programme and hopes that these initiatives will create conducive environment
for doing R&D in the country at par with international standards and yield desired results.
(Para 18.4)

15
Action Taken
The Department thankfully accepts the appreciation of two schemes by the Committee and assures
that it will take all steps to ensure that these initiatives create conducive environment for doing Research
and Development (R&D) in the country at par with international standards and yield desired results.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply and would like to be apprised about new initiatives
taken for Research and Development during Demands for Grants 2018-19.
POPULARISATION OF TECHNOLOGIES DEVELOPED
Recommendation
The Committee is of the opinion that the pace of dissemination of fruits of technology to the end
user needs to be expedited. The Committee, therefore, recommends that Department of Science and
Technology, being the nodal department of scientific department responsible for consideration and policy
formulation, in collaboration with other scientific Departments, should consider developing an institutional
mechanism exclusively for marketing and popularization of technologies developed by various scientific
departments, so that the benefits of these technologies are actually utilised by the people for whom those
are intended. (Para 19.2)
Action Taken
The invaluable views and suggestions of Hon'ble members of the Committee are well taken and will
form the basis of the endeavours of the DST in future. SEED Division is taking requisite steps to
customize and deliver need based technologies at users level by engaging S&T knowledge institutions and
field agencies for effective technology delivery at the grassroots level.
DST is taking appropriate steps to collaborate with other scientific Departments and other agencies
to popularize and commercialize technologies developed by them to facilitate actual utilization of such
technology packages for the benefit of our people, particularly the poorest, weakest and underprivileged.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply. The Committee is hopeful that with necessary
support of the Department, the lead Ministries/Departments will popularise technologies developed
for benefit of the poorest, weakest and underprivileged people of the country.
UTILISATION OF SOCIALLY USEFUL TECHNOLOGIES READY FOR COMMERCIAL USE
DEVELOPED BY SCIENTIFIC DEPARTMENTS WITH SCHEMES/PROGRAMMES OF MINISTRIES/
DEPARTMENTS
Recommendation
The Committee welcomes the joint collaborative steps taken by DST in collaboration with Department
of Heavy Industries, Ministries of Railways and Urban Development and hopes that these collaborations
will fill the critical gaps. The Committee is of the view that the Department should leave no stone
unturned in assisting the lead Ministries/Departments for the success of these programmes.
(Para 20.2)

16
Action Taken
The Department is thankful to the Committee for its appreciation of DST's collaborative efforts with
other Ministries and ensures that such collaborations would be further intensified to help/lead Ministries/
Departments to effectively implement their programmes.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply and hopes that collaborations with other Departments/
Ministries will help the Department come out of the silo and lead to popularisation of technologies
developed by Scientific Departments.
Recommendation
The Committee feels that yet another effective way of gainfully utilizing the socially beneficial
technologies ready for commercial use could be to integrate them with the related schemes/programmes
being run by various Ministries/Departments of Government of India. All that the Department of Science
and Technology needs to do is to reach out to the concerned Ministries/ Departments and to impress upon
them to integrate into their programmes/projects, these proven technologies. For example, providing
potable drinking water in rural and urban areas has turned out to be a formidable challenge for the
Ministries of Drinking Water and Sanitation and Urban Development during natural Disaster which has
affected country in a big way in recent past. After such disaster, problem of drinking water affects people
in a big way. CSIR has developed Reverse Osmosis Mounted Bus. This technology can be of great help
to affected States facing natural disaster. Similarly, Department of Atomic Energy has proven technology
for water purification sludge hygienisation and water desalination, which costs as less as 6 Paisa per
liter. This technology can easily be replicated at all those places facing safe potable water problems or
where underground water is contaminated with arsenic or fluoride, etc. both in urban and rural areas
of the country by getting it linked with Rural Water Mission and in the urban areas with the Urban Local
Government Bodies. (Para 20.3)
Action Taken
The valuable views and suggestions of Hon'ble members of the Committee are well taken and will
form the basis of the endeavours of DST in future.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply and would like to be apprised of the action taken
in this regard.
Recommendation
Similarly, Department of Science and Technology can help power deficient states with transferring
solar LED bulbs, Surya Jyoti which saves power. Milk adulteration checking technology developed by
Departments of Science and Technology and Scientific and Industrial Research can be shared with State
Governments and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. The Committee believes that by doing so the
Department would be able to disseminate socially beneficial technologies ready for commercial use in
a big way and their benefits would also easily reach to the people and the society. This will also help
the Ministry of Science and Technology earn creditability and goodwill. (Para 20.4)

17
Action Taken
The invaluable views and suggestions of Hon'ble members of the Committee are well taken and will
form the basis of endeavors of DST in future. The Department would make concerted efforts to
disseminate socially beneficial technologies ready for commercial use as in the case of Surya Jyoti by
demonstrating its utility in different States through adaptive Research and Development and by engaging
its partner agencies.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply and would like to be apprised of the action taken
in this regard.
Recommendation
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department of Science and Technology being the
nodal Department for Science, Technology and Innovation should act on the lines being suggested by
the Committee and initiate interaction with the concerned Ministries/Departments to convince them of
the relevance and efficacy of technologies developed by Scientific Departments within a given timeframe.
The Committee also recommends that the Department should take all possible measures to take the
technologies to the people as technology lying in the labyrinth of laboratory is good for nothing. Its real
success lies in its application for the benefit of the poorest and the weakest. (Para 20.5)
Action Taken
The invaluable views and suggestions of Hon'ble members of the Committee are well taken and will
form the basis of the endeavours of the DST in future. SEED Division will continue to take all possible
steps to connect with other Government Departments and organizations to develop/deliver technology
packages for societal benefits, particularly benefiting the poorest and the weakest.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.

INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairperson of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and
Technology, Environment and Forests, having been authorised by the Committee to present the Report
on its behalf, present this Three Hundred Fifth Report on the Action Taken by the Department of
Scientific and Industrial Research on the recommendations/observations contained in the Two Hundred
Ninety-seventh Report of the Committee on Demands for Grants (2017-2018) of the Department of
Scientific and Industrial Research, which was presented/laid in the both the Houses of Parliament on 31st
March, 2017.
2. There were thirty-two recommendations/observations in the Two Hundred Ninety-seventh Report
of the Committee. Action Taken Notes on the recommendations/observations of the Committee were
received from the Department on 20th July, 2017 and 11th December, 2017.
3. In the meeting held on 1st January, 2018 the Committee considered the draft Report and adopted
the same.
  N
EW D ELHI; ANAND SHARMA

REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Scientific and
Industrial Research on the recommendations/observations contained in the Two Hundred Ninety-seventh
Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology,
Environment and Forests on the Demands for Grants (2017-18) of the Department of Scientific and
Industrial Research, (Ministry of Science and Technology) presented to both the Houses of Parliament
on 31st March, 2017. There were thirty-two recommendations/observations in the Report of the Committee.
Action Taken note on the recommendations of the Committee were received from the Department on
20th July and 11th December, 2017.
The Committee's recommendations, action taken note thereon and comments of the Committee on
the Action Taken by the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research, are set out in the following
paragraphs:—
FINANCIAL  ACHIEVEMENTS  OF  THE  DEPARTMENT
Recommendation
The Committee observes that financial performance of the Department has been satisfactory in the
past few years. However, the Committee notes that the Department has utilized 
` 3203.45 crore (upto
31.01.2017) against the allocated amount of ` 4062.80 crore only during 2016-17 which shows that
proper and timely planning for utilization of the allocated fund was not done. In view of this, the
Committee recommends that the Department must have proper and robust monitoring mechanism for
utilizing the allocated funds so that optimum utilization of allocated funds may be ensured .(Para 2.2)
Action Taken
Utilization of allocated funds till 31.01.2017 was 78.84%. An amount of ` 4051.67 crore was
utilized during the full F.Y . 2016-17, which amounts to 99.73% utilization of allocated funds.
The department notes the observation of the Committee for optimum utilization of funds and shall
strive for even better utilization next year.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
REQUEST AND JUSTIFICATION FOR ADDITIONAL BUDGETARY ALLOCATION FOR
FINANCIAL YEAR 2017-18
Recommendation
In view of the above submissions of the Department, the Committee feels that request for the
enhancement in the budgetary allocation to the tune of 
` 500.00 crore for the financial year 2017-18
is fully justified and the matter should be taken up by with the concerned Ministry/Department vigorously.

2
The Committee also observes that scientific institutions like CSIR should not suffer due to lack of money
especially in the cutting edge national labs which are involved in various researches in the field of
science. (Para 3.5)
Action Taken
The Department is thankful to the Committee for its recommendation for enhancing the budgetary
allocation.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
SCHEMES  OF  THE DEPARTMENT OF SCIENTIFIC AND INDUSTRIAL RESEARCH
Recommendation
The Committee notes that there has been gross under-utilization of allocated resources not only
during 2016-17 but in the past too, in all the four Schemes viz. Promoting Innovations in Individuals,
Start-ups and MSMEs (PRISM), Patent Acquisition and Collaborative Research and Technology
Development (P ACE), Building Industrial Research and Development (BIRD) and Access to Knowledge
for Creation of Innovative Capacity and Dissemination (A2K) of the Department. The reasons for under-
utilization of allocated funds have also not been given by the Department. Because of under-utilizations,
allocation at BE stage for 2017-18 in some of the said schemes have been reduced substantially. The
Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the Department should strengthen its administrative and
monitoring mechanism for utilizing the allocated resources right from beginning and evaluation be done
in each quarter. (Para 4.11)
Action Taken
The reasons for under-utilization of allocated funds in the DSIR schemes on PRISM, PACE, BIRD
and A2k+ have been: delay in formulation and approval of guidelines and standard operating procedures
of the schemes; and slow pace of expenditure by the project implementing agencies in spite of rigorous
follow-up by the department.
The department takes note of the recommendations of the Committee for strengthening the monitoring
mechanism for optimum utilization of the allocated resources during 2017-18. Subsequent to obtaining
approval for continuation of the schemes for 2017-20, the department shall monitor the utilization of
allocated resources by means of a Committee comprising of representatives of Group Heads of the
schemes and Financial Adviser.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the steps initiated by the Department would
yield the desired results.
PROGRAMME  FOR  DEVELOPMENT OF  TECHNOLOGIES FOR COMMERCIALISATION
(PDTC)
Recommendation
The Committee notes that NRDC plays a significant role in transfer of technologies emanating from
R&D laboratories and its operation covers entire spectrum of technologies. However, the Committee

3
expresses its deep concern over under-utilization of allocated amount during 2016-17. The Committee
hopes that proper planning would be done for optimum utilization of allocated amount during 2017-18.
The Committee further recommends that NRDC should have close co-ordination and constant interactions
with CSIR-labs in order to promote, develop and commercialize the technology emanating from various
labs so that it could reach the masses of the country. (Para 5.6)
Action Taken
NRDC was allocated an amount of ` 2.75 crore by DSIR under the scheme on "Programme for
Development of Technologies for Commercialization (PDTC)" during 2016-17. It has utilized ` 2.35
crore, which amounts to 85.45% utilization of the allocated funds. The department notes the observation
of the Committee for optimum utilization of funds by NRDC during 2017-18 and shall closely follow-
up with NRDC in this regard.
Further, NRDC has renewed the umbrella MoU with CSIR as well as signed MoUs with a number
of CSIR labs to commercialize their technologies for reaching out to the masses.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
CENTRAL ELECTRONICS LTD. (CEL)
Recommendation
The Committee feels that Department should be more proactive in utilizing the allocated amount
during 2017-18 in order to attain the objectives of CEL by strengthening the monitoring mechanism.
(Para 6.6)
Action Taken
The Department thankfully notes the observations of the Committee and shall take necessary steps
for full utilization of allocated amount of ` 9 crore to CEL during 2017-18. It is stated that ` 6.25 crore
has already been released till September, 2017.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
CONSULTANCY DEVELOPMENT CENTRE (CDC)
Recommendation
The Committee hopes that no cut or reduction in the allocated amount would be done during
2017-18 at RE stage for smooth and effective functioning of CDC. (Para 7.4)
Action Taken
The Department thankfully notes the observations of the Committee and is hopeful that no cut or
reduction in the allocated amount of ` 2 crore to CDC during 2017-18 would be done at the RE stage,
since ` 1.00 crore has already been released till September, 2017.

4
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
COUNCIL OF SCIENTIFIC AND INDUSTRIAL RESEARCH (CSIR)
Recommendation
The Committee notes and appreciates the efforts of CSIR in publishing large number of research
papers in International SCI journals every year. However, the Committee observes that good work done
by the CSIR in the form of research papers do not translate into sustainable technologies for use of the
masses. Hence, the Committee recommends that Department should make all out efforts so that research
and inventions may be translated into sustainable technologies. The Committee further recommends that
the scientific journals/papers/publications etc. should come out on time and with high standards.
(Para 8.6)
Action Taken
The Department is thankful for the appreciation indicated by the Committee. The Department likes
to inform the Committee that the translation of published papers into technologies takes time.
However, the Department takes Note of the concern of the Committee and will make all efforts to
publish scientific journals/papers etc. on time and with high standards.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that there would be no let up in the efforts of
the Department on this count.
NATIONAL LABORATORIES SCHEME
Recommendation
The Committee observes that the National Laboratories Scheme of the Department is very significant
in improving lives of citizens of the country through scientific advancement. The Committee notes that
during 2016-17 only 
` 2948.50 crore was utilized under National Laboratories scheme till 31.01.2017
as against allocation (R.E.) of ` 3713.06 crore by the Department. At the one hand, the Department
is pursuing for more allocation but on the other hand allocated amount could not be spent fully by the
Department. Therefore, the Committee recommends that Department should have a proper monitoring and
planning mechanism in place so that allocated amount must be utilized fully during 2017-18.
(Para 9.3)
Action Taken
The Department takes Note of the recommendation for having a proper monitoring and planning
mechanism for full utilization of the allocated amount during 2017-18.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like to be informed of the action taken by the
Department.

5
Recommendation
The Committee also feels that creation of national labs under this scheme and other significant
activities may further be extended in those States where its presence is negligible especially in States like
Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh etc. (Para 9.4)
Action Taken
The Department likes to apprise the Committee that CSIR has its significant presence in Uttar
Pradesh with four constituent laboratories namely CSIR-Central Institute of Medicinal and Aromatic
Plants (CSIR-CIMAP), CSIR-National Botanical Research Institute (CSIR-NBRI), CSIR-Central Drug
Research Institute (CSIR-CDRI) and CSIR-Indian Institute of Toxicology Research as well as Central
Institute of Mining and Fuel Research, Dhanbad in Jharkhand and CSIR-Advanced Materials and Processes
Research Institute (CSIR-AMPRI) in Bhopal (MP).
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
EXAMINATION OF SOME OF THE CSIR-LABS/INSTITUTES/ORGANISATIONS
Recommendation
The Committee commends the role of NPL for its glorious achievements in the past in the field of
scientific research activities and emerging as a leading national institution for research in a whole gamut
of areas in the physical science. The Committee hopes that NPL would be able to excel in its field and
also strive hard for its contribution towards nation building. (Para 10.8)
Action Taken
The Department likes to convey its gratitude to the Committee for its appreciation and further
efforts shall be continued by CSIR-NPL to excel in its field.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the efforts of the Department would yield
the desired results.
CSIR-NATIONAL AEROSPACE LABORATORIES (NAL), BENGALURU
Recommendation
The Committee observes that CSIR-NAL is a premier research institution of the country and, over
the last five decades, NAL has successfully contributed towards the growth of aerospace activities in the
country which has resulted in achieving expertise in many disciplines of the aerospace technology. The
Committee appreciates that the Scientific and Technological research of NAL which has helped the nation
in overcoming technological challenges, without compromising the confidentiality of the strategic data.
The Committee recommends that CSIR-NAL should identify its future challenges, continue its research,
scientific and technical work and its contribution to the civil, strategic and aerospace sector.
(Para 11.5)

6
Action Taken
The Department is thankful for the appreciation indicated by the Committee by the Committee and
also takes note of the recommendation.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like to be apprised the steps taken in the above
direction.
Recommendation
The Committee is also constrained to note that CSIR-NAL's proposal for funding of 70-seater
Regional Transport Aircraft has been awaiting the Government's approval since the last three years. The
Committee recommends that DSIR should immediately take the required action in the matter and ensure
that approval for the project is granted at the earliest so that further action in respect of the project can
be taken up by the CSIR-NAL. (Para 11.6)
Action Taken
The Department takes Note of the recommendation.
Comments
The Committee notes that the Department has not furnished any action taken in the
matter and would like to be informed of the same.
CSIR-FOURTH PARADIGM INSTITUTE (4PI), BENGALURU
Recommendation
The Committee commends the various activities of CSIR-Fourth Paradigm Institute, especially the
High Performance Computing Facility. The Committee, however, recommends that DSIR should closely
look into the affairs of CSIR-4PI and ensure that the shadow of factors which slowed down the progress
of the Institute does not adversely affect its functioning for long. The Committee hopes that CSIR-4PI
would continue the good R&D in supercomputing and cyber security research. The Committee recommends
that 4PI should strengthen the present modelling and simulation capability with focus on earth system
and hazard by bringing in new capability in data and computational science. (Para 12.4)
Action Taken
The Department is thankful to the Committee for its appreciation.
It may please be noted that further steps have been taken by CSIR-4PI to enhance the computing
facility by additional 127 Teraflops during 2017. With C-DAC as partner, proposal is now in place to take
forward the cyber security research. Steps have also been initiated to further strengthen the modeling
and simulation capability.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.

7
CSIR-CENTRAL GLASS & CERAMIC RESEARCH INSTITUTE (CGCRI), KOLKATA
Recommendation
The Chairperson suggested that all the laboratories involved in manufacturing these membranes to
put it on a single platform and then as the Government of India should direct that municipalities, coming
under urban planning, all must access this platform. The Chairperson also suggested that Government
could have a forum to put all the developments of these labs in Doordarshan, after taking steps to protect
the intellectual property. (Para 13.9)
Action Taken
The Department appreciates the suggestions provided by the Committee. It is informed that CSIR
is evaluating the feasibility of a Mission mode project on Water.
Comments
The Committee notes that the Department has not furnished actual action taken on the
observations contained in the above para and would like to know the response of the Department.
Recommendation
The Committee notes the activities and achievements of CGCRI in the field of ceramic and glass
research in order to maximize the economic, environmental and social benefit for people of the country.
The Committee feels that Department should take proactive measures so that technologies developed by
the CSIR Scientific Institutions like CGCRI reaches the masses faster through industries/ companies. The
Committee also recommends that proper mechanism must be in place for disseminating the activities and
achievements of scientific labs at national level by involving universities and initiating discussion and
interactions with State Governments and also through media. (Para 13.11)
Action Taken
The Department has been disseminating information on its technologies through various events such
as:
1. CSIR Technofest held at Pragati Maidan, New Delhi
2. Indian Science Festival organized at CSIR-NPL
3. CSIR-Industry meets
4. Starting of Incubation Centre and Technology Parks
5. Advertisement through various media on a regular basis
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation
The Committee appreciates the work done by CGCRI by using ceramic membrane technology for
water purification which removes arsenic and iron from the contaminated water making it potable. The

8
Committee notes that mostly these plants have been installed in West Bengal besides some other States
like Sikkim and North- East States. The Committee feels that this technology should be extended in other
States also including far remote places like Lakshadweep islands. Further, the Committee recommends
that DSIR should co-ordinate with all scientific laboratories which are involved in manufacturing these
membranes to put it on a single platform and then concerned Ministries/ Departments should direct that
municipalities, coming under urban planning, must access this platform in order to provide clean and
safe water to its citizens. (Para 13.12)
Action Taken
The Department takes Note of the recommendations by the Committee and efforts will be made
for evolving suitable mechanisms for wider dissemination and deployment.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like be further apprised in this regard during
examination of Demand for Grants 2018-19 of the Department.
CSIR - INDIAN INSTITUTE OF CHEMICAL BIOLOGY (IICB), KOLKATA
Recommendation
The Committee felt that a number of Biotechnology related inventions have come up but has not
gone as people program. NRDC is the right agency that can assimilate and initiate our up gradations
and asked about steps taken in this regard. (Para 14.7)
Action Taken
CSIR-IICB has entered an MoU with NRDC to commercialize all potential technologies. CSIR-IICB
is engaging companies who have shown interest in the technologies for co-development and licensing.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that that the efforts being made by the Department
would yield the desired results.
CSIR - INDIAN INSTITUTE OF CHEMICAL BIOLOGY (IICB), KOLKATA
Recommendation
During the meeting, the Committee was of the view that in both presentations there are two major
disconnects, firstly a disconnect between work done in the labs and industry and secondly between work
done in the labs and universities. The Committee felt that the pharmaceutical industry is going in one
direction which is quite unfortunate. About 10 year back we developed significant pharmaceutical
industries. After the FDI policy, things changed. Today R&D of pharmaceutical company is generally
poor in the country. The Committee recommends that since, CSIR being the eyes and ears of the
Government in R&D, it should make efforts to remove disconnect between the R&D and industry,
particularly for the benefit of Indians. (Para 14.12)

9
Action Taken
CSIR laboratories who are working in the area of healthcare research are taking steps to engage
with many pharmaceutical companies. MoUs are also being signed for contract research, joint development
and technology licensing etc.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation
The Committee appreciates the good work done by IICB in the field of chemical and biological
sciences, and extensive research work done in containing diseases such as cholera, developing leishmaniasis
detection kit and achievements made in translating medicine for asthma namely Asmon, Prostalyn,
compounds from Paan leaf, mentoring National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research
(NIPER), Kolkata and futuristic research focused on Dengue and Alzheimer's etc. The Committee feels
that these research outcomes/findings should be disseminated all over the country involving various
stakeholders and universities so that general public at large may benefit. (Para 14.17)
Action Taken
CSIR-IICB has taken initiative in skill development program to provide skill training for about 500
people on various aspects of skill. CSIR-IICB is training NIPER MS students in their Project work.
The Department takes Note of the recommendations by the Committee and efforts will be made
for evolving suitable mechanisms for wider dissemination of research findings amongst various stakeholders.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation
The Committee also observes that a number of bio-technology related research and inventions of
IICB have not reached to the masses in the absence of proper agencies or mechanism with regard to
technology transfer. In view of this, the Committee recommends that National Research Development
Corporation (NRDC) of the Department should be engaged by doing MoU in order to promote, develop
and commercialize the technology emanating from IICB at the earliest. (Para 14.18)
Action Taken
CSIR-IICB has entered into a MoU with NRDC to translate its technologies and to connect with
the right type of pharmaceutical companies inter-alia its own effort to connect with companies. The
Department would like to inform the Committee that CSIR has renewed its MoU with NRDC for
enhancing commercialization of its technologies. Further number of other CSIR laboratories have also
signed MoU separately with NRDC for commercializing and marketing of their technologies.

10
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that there would be no let up in the efforts of
the Department in this direction.
Recommendation
The Committee further observes that both the above said institutions of CSIR i.e. Central Glass and
Ceramic Research Institute (CGCRI) and Indian Institute of Chemical Biology (IICB) have two major
disconnects, firstly work done in the labs and industry and secondly work done in the labs and universities.
The committee, therefore, recommends that there should be much more interactions between CSIR labs
and the industries as well as Universities. (Para 14.19)
Action Taken
CSIR-IICB and CSIR-CGCRI has initiated steps to have better connectivity with industries, as
suggested by the parliamentary delegation. This is done through NRDC and also through in-house
mechanism. The visits of a number of university students are arranged to CSIR-IICB so that they get
exposure to the laboratory facilities and also to connect with the work done at the laboratory from time
to time.
CSIR and constituent laboratories are interacting with industries through Industrial Meets, Workshops,
etc. Also CSIR are organizing Open Day, summer training etc. for providing opportunity to academic
institutions for closer interactions.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
NATIONAL  S&T HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME
Recommendation
The Committee welcomes the enhancement in allocations for this Scheme from 
`300 cr. in 2016-
17 to `325 cr. in BE 2017-18. However, the Committee takes serious note that during 2016-17, an
amount of ` 225 cr. only (upto 31.01.2017) was spent against the allocated RE of ` 300 cr. which clearly
states that physical targets could not be achieved fully and many of the deserving students might have
been denied the opportunities to get the fellowships/ Scholarships. The Committee, therefore, recommends
that in future, the Department should be more careful in utilizing the allocated amount. (Para 15.8)
Action Taken
Noted for action in future. However, the expenditure under the Scheme depends on the submission
of Fellowship grant-in-aid claim bill along with Utilization Certificate (UC) and Statement of Expenditure
(SE) by the grantee institutions. The grantee institutions will be requested to submit the fellowship grant-
in-aid claim bill in time to enable CSIR to fully utilize the allocated funds. Further the efforts have been
made to increase the number of fellowships. The number of JRF-NET award has been enhanced to more
than 4000 (4038) through the NET conducted in June and December 2016 compared to 2369 awarded

11
during 2015-16. Similarly, the number of SRF is increased to 518 in 2016-17 compared to 218 during
previous financial year.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation
The Committee also feels that to catch young students and nurture, groom and develop them into
budding scientists, it is imperative that a concerted and co-ordinated strategy is made on a long- term
basis. Since, CSIR has vast chain of scientific labs and the biggest institution as employer of scientists;
it has to actively play a major role in this direction. Just by awarding some fellowships/ Scholarships,
this mammoth task is not going to be accomplished. Therefore, the Committee recommends that the
Department must come out with some concrete proposals to trap, harness and retain human resources in
the field of science. (Para 15.9)
Action Taken
To harness and train the human resources in the field of science, CSIR has modified the eligibility
criteria for its CSIR-UGC National Eligibility Test (NET) for Junior Research Fellowship (JRF) wherein
graduates in science and engineering can also appear in the NET and may take the benefit of fellowship
for pursuing doctoral research in the field of science. CSIR has a JRF-GATE scheme for GATE qualified
engineering and GPAT qualified pharmaceutical graduates to pursue research through a suitable PhD
programme in AcSIR or in any other institution. Also, CSIR awards Senior Research Fellowships in
Science, Engineering and Medicinal and Pharmaceutical Sciences through interview mode to young
talented students who have two years research experience. Such steps will help in accomplishing the task
of catching the young students and nurture, groom and develop them into the budding scientists. Further,
21% of total research fellows (about 7000) supported by CSIR are pursuing their research work in CSIR
laboratories.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that CSIR would continue its efforts in this
direction in right earnest.
FILING AND GRANT OF PATENTS
Recommendation
The Committee appreciates the efforts of CSIR in obtaining patents in India and abroad. However,
the Committee feels that ratio in respect of Patents filed and Patents granted in India and abroad is
not encouraging. The Committee, therefore, recommends that Department should have constant vigil on
this front and also the matter may be taken up vigorously with National Biodiversity Authority (NBA)
for clearance of around 150 patents, in order to file the same with the Indian Patent Office in the field
of Biological Sciences, at the earliest. (Para 16.4)

12
Action Taken
The Department takes note of the recommendation.
Comments
The Committee notes that the Department has not furnished any concrete reply to its
recommendation and would like to know the action taken in respect of recommendation of the
Committee.
WORLD RANKING OF CSIR
Recommendation
The Committee notes with satisfaction that CSIR has improved its world ranking among Government
institutions as well as its overall global ranking. However, the Committee observes that CSIR is still far
behind amongst the globally benchmarked scientific organisations in the world. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that in order to place India in the list of the top countries in the scientific world, CSIR
should aim to become amongst at least first 10 global organisations in its field and it should strive hard
to achieve that ranking. (Para 17.3)
Action Taken
The Department is thankful for the appreciation indicated by the Committee and takes note of the
recommendation.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
PROJECTS/SCHEMES IN NORTH - EASTERN STATES
Recommendation
The Committee notes the initiatives taken by the Department in the form of various projects/
schemes being run in the North-Eastern States of the country which will bring the qualitative changes
in the lives of the people of that area and also generate employment opportunities. However, the
Committee feels that lot more is needed to be done in order to augment the incomes and improve the
quality of lives of millions of people geographically spread across the North-Eastern States of the
country. (Para 18.6)
Action Taken
The Department thankfully notes the observations of the Committee. CSIR and NRDC are being
requested to undertake projects and programmes that would augment the incomes and improve the
quality of lives of millions of people geographically spread across the North-Eastern States of the
country.
Comments
The Committee note the reply and would like to know the steps taken by CSIR and NRDC
in this regards.

13
SKILL DEVELOPMENT
Recommendation
The Committee appreciates the efforts of the Department in this matter and hopes that it will yield
desired results and will go a long way in respect of social upliftment of down-trodden persons of the
society. However, the Committee feels that merely running new skill programs in the areas of Leather
Processing Technology, Industrial Maintenance Engineering, Mechatronics, Instrumentation, Battery
maintenance, Internet of Things, Advance Manufacturing Technology, etc. is not enough unless those
skilled persons are employed or integrated in the respective industries. Therefore, the Committee recommends
that Department should have linkages with various industries as well Ministries/Departments so that
these skilled persons could get suitable employment and sustain their livelihoods. (Para 19.4)
Action Taken
Many of the new skill programs implemented by the department are relevant to the industries in
different regions of the country to enhance employability/placement of trained persons. The programs
are also offering them entrepreneurial prospects.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
CSIR'S ROYALTY AND EARNINGS OF DEPARTMENT BY TECHNOLOGY TRANSFER
Recommendation
The Committee observes that income of the Department from royalty component is very low as
compared to the huge investment of the Government on account of research/innovations/R&D etc.
vis-a-vis profit earned by the private companies/industries by making commercial use of technologies
developed by the Department. In view of this, the Committee recommends that MoU should be signed
with the companies/industries for fixing royalty component while making technology transfer/inventions
for allowing its product for commercial utilization so that Department could be financially self reliant
in every aspect and invest in R&D. (Para 20.4)
Action Taken
The Department thankfully notes the observations of the Committee. MoUs signed with companies/
industries at the time of sanctioning technology development and commercialization projects do fix the
royalty percentage to be paid by industries but the amount of royalty realized depends upon the actual
commercialization and the earnings made by companies, which varies as per the prevailing market and
technology scenario. CSIR has also put in place new guidelines for technology transfer Utilization of
Knowledgebase-2017. The department endeavors to maintain a balance between its objectives of promotional
role for technological up-gradation of industry and to ensure that more and more royalty accrues to
Government, which can be ploughed back into further R&D.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.

14
Recommendation
The Committee, therefore, recommends that investment in R&D must be increased so that research
work may be taken up at large scale and more and more representatives of industries/companies should
be motivated for making investment in R&D of the Scientific Ministries/Departments of the country.
(Para 20.6)
Action Taken
The Department thankfully notes the observations of the Committee. The Department through its
industrial R&D Promotion Programme and other programmes continuously endeavors to drive more and
more industries/companies to take up collaborative R&D projects with Scientific Ministries/Departments.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation
The Committee further is of the opinion that instead of giving the technologies to private companies/
industries in the first instances, option for exploring transfer of technologies to Public Sector companies
may be explored which could be beneficial for both i.e. Department as well as Public Sector companies.
In order to achieve this goal, the Committee recommends that more tie-ups between the Department and
Public Sector companies/institutions should be done. (Para 20.7)
Action Taken
The Department thankfully notes the observations of the Committee and make endeavors to make
more tie ups.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the endeavours of the Department would yield the desired
results.
DUPLICATION IN RESEARCH WORK/ TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT
Recommendation
However, the Committee feels that this shows some sort of lack of co-ordination and consultation
between the various Scientific Ministries/Departments of the country. The Committee, therefore, recommends
that a mechanism should be evolved for having a constant and broad consultation/
co-ordination amongst the various Scientific Ministries/Departments about the areas/fields of research so
that time, energy, money, manpower and other resources of the country may be utilized optimally.
(Para 21.3)
Action Taken
The Department notes the observations of the Committee. Actions and targets of various scientific
Ministries/Departments are continuously monitored during the meetings of 'Sectoral Group of Secretaries'
taken periodically by the Cabinet Secretary. This ensures optimum utilization of all resources.

15
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
AW ARENESS AND OUTREACH PROGRAMME OF THE DEPARTMENT
Recommendation
The Committee during its meeting held on 15th February, 2017 had also observed that people of
the country including elected representatives are not aware of the excellent work in the field of Science
being done by the Department or much about the Department itself which may be beneficial for a very
big segment of the society like farmers, fishermen, students, research scholars etc. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the Department should prepare a comprehensive awareness programme with
a calendar of events using social media platforms, radio, television etc. meant for researchers, academia,
farmers, industries, students and general public but most importantly for all the elected representatives
right from district level i.e. Members of Zila Panchayats, Legislative Assemblies and Councils and
Members of Parliament. The Committee strongly feels that elected representatives can play an important
role in making their constituents aware of scientific development and ultimately developing scientific
temperament in the public at large. (Para 22.2)
Action Taken
The Department notes the observations of the Committee. It is submitted that an exhibition on
'Scientific achievements and technologies ready to be deployed" by all the Scientific Ministries/Departments
was organized by DSIR/CSIR at the Parliament House Annexe during the Monsoon Session, 2017 of the
Parliament. The exhibition, organized at the behest of 'Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science &
Technology, Environment & Forests' was visited by a large number of MPs and Ministers, who appreciated
the innovative products/processes and systems showcased by various scientific ministries.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and would like the Department to take measures to initiate
comprehensive awareness programmes for other stakeholders mentioned in the recommendations
as well.

REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Space on the
recommendations/observations contained in the Two Hundred and Ninety eighth Report of the Department-
related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science & Technology, Environment & Forests on the
Demands for Grants (2017-18) of the Department of Space, which was presented to both the Houses
of Parliament on 31st March, 2017. There were forty recommendations/observations in the Report of
the Committee. Action Taken Note on the recommendations of the Committee was received from the
Department on 31st July, 2017. The Committee, on examination of Action Taken Notes, is not satisfied
with action taken by the Department in respect of one recommendation (para 5.3) and would like the
Department to take further action thereon as indicated in the Report.
The Committee's recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee on the
action taken by the Department of Space are set out in the succeeding paragraphs:-
ANALYSIS OF THE PERFORMANCE OF THE DEPARTMENT DURING THE 12TH FIVE YEAR
PLAN PERIOD:
Recommendation
The Committee expresses its satisfaction over the capacity of the Department to utilise the funds
made available for the whole of 12th Five Year Plan period. The financial performance of the Department
also indicates that had the Department been given the full amount of 
` 39750.00 crore as projected by
the Department in its Indicative Plan Outlay for the 12th Five Year Plan period, the Department would
not only have utilised the fund fully but made most out of it also. (Para 3.4)
Action Taken
The observation of the Committee are Noted. The Department will strive to continue the good
financial performance in coming years too.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department.
COMMUNICATION SATELLITE:
Recommendation
The Committee notes that against a target of 14 communication satellites as planned by the
Department to be realised during the 12th Plan period, the Department could manage to launch only
7 communication satellites viz., GSAT-10, GSAT-14, GSAT-16, GSAT-7, GSAT-6, GSAT-15 and GSAT-
18 during the 12th Plan period. The Committee feels that the Department could have done better to
realise its fixed targets of 14 communication satellites. The Committee is of the considered opinion that
keeping the increasing demand of the transponders for meeting requirements of the country, it is imperative
that the Department should accordingly strategise its action plan so as to keep pace with the increasing
demand and achieve the targets set for the purpose in a timeframe manner. (Para 4.4)

2
Action Taken
During 12th Five Year Plan period, 14 communication satellites were planned by the Department of
which 7 were realised. In addition, ISRO has realised 3 more communication satellites off late viz. GSAT-
9 (South Asia Satellite), GSAT-17 and GSAT-19 (High throughput satellite). Further, ISRO has worked
on realisation of GSAT-6A satellite which is getting ready for launch. The Department will make all
efforts to meet the specific target and has already accelerated its plan to realise more number of
communication satellites, thereby narrowing the demand-supply gap for communication transponders.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department. However, the Committee feels that the
Department needs to further strengthen its action and work in tandem with the other concerned
stake holders, so as to cater to the increasing demand of the communication transponders in the
country.
Recommendation
The Committee further notes that four more communication satellites (GSAT-9/South Asia Satellite,
GSAT-17, GSAT-19 and GSAT-11) are in advance stage of realisation and are planned to be launched
during 2017 by the Department. The Committee hopes that the task undertaken by the Department of
launching these four communication satellites will be achieved within the stipulated time. The Committee
hopes that the launch of these four communication satellites will further help the Department to bridge
the gap between demand and supply of the transponders in the country. (Para 4.5)
Action Taken
Out of the four communication satellites mentioned above, three satellites viz GSAT-9/South Asia
Satellite, GSAT-19 and GSAT-17 have been launched during the first quarter of 2017-18. Realisation of
GSAT-11 communication satellite is under assembly, integration and testing. The satellite is targeted for
launch by end of 2017 and efforts to secure the launch slot from M/s. Arianespace are under progress.
GSA T-11 & GSA T-19 together will provide more than 20 Gbps throughput capacity for interactive
telecommunications services.
In addition, GSAT-6A communication satellite carrying S-band transponders is planned to be launched
during second half of 2017-18.
Comments
The Committee accepts the reply of the Department and is hopeful that all the related work
in respect of GSAT-11 and GSAT-6A will be completed within the stipulated time and these
communication satellites will be launched as per their time schedule.
SATELLITE BASED NA VIGATION:
Recommendation
The Committee notes the achievements of the Department in satellite based navigation during the
12th Plan period. The Committee, however, is surprised that the Department has not mentioned anything
about the progress made in the formulation of Indian Satellite Navigation Policy as envisioned by the

3
Department during the 12th Plan period. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department
should furnish a current status note in this connection at the earliest for the consideration of the
Committee. (Para 5.3)
Action Taken
Deliberations on the utilisation of the NavIC for civil as well as strategic services and production
of the user receivers & devices are under progress. All the relevant Government Departments and
Ministries like Ministry of Communications, Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology, Ministry
of Defence, and Department of Space etc. are engaged in the discussions. The activity is expected to
be concluded shortly. Department plans to bring up the draft Satellite Navigation Policy for discussions
and approval by end 2017.
Comments
The Committee finds the reply of the Department intangible as the Department appears to
have been failed in completing the primary work i.e. consultation process with the relevant stake
holders during the last five years. The Committee, therefore, would like to be informed of the
progress in a matter.
Recommendation
The Committee observes that against the budgetary allocation of 
` 90.00 crore in RE 2016-17 under
the component 'National Navigation System (NSS)', the Department could only utilise ` 67.18 crore upto
January, 2017 which is 74.64 percent of the total allocation. The Committee expresses its concerns about
this underutilisation of the funds. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should
exercise financial prudence and make sure that the allocation made on account of NSS is utilised fully
and optimally. (Para 5.4)
Action Taken
As on January 2017, the expenditure under the component 'Navigation Satellite System (NSS)' was
Rs 67.18 Crore. However, at the end of March 2017, the expenditure under the programme was Rs 81.73
Crore which is about 91% of the RE allocations. The marginal under-utilisation was due to phasing out
of expenditure towards major civil works for ground segment realisation to next financial year. The
Department shall exercise caution and optimally utilise the funds allocated in 2017-18.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department.
EARTH OBSERV ATION AND ATMOSPHERIC SCIENCES PROGRAMME
Recommendation
The Committee, while noting the targets achieved by the Department under the Earth Observation
and Atmospheric Sciences Programme during the 12th Plan period, expresses its dissatisfaction over the
fact that against the allocated amount of 
` 50.00 crore in RE 2016-17 under the component 'Resourcesat-

4
2A', the Department could actually utilise ` 38.03 crore only which is just 76.06 percent of the allocated

SPACE TRANSPORTATION SYSTEMS:
Recommendation
The Committee notes achievements of the Department in the field of Space Transportation. The
Committee, however, observes that in order to capture the global market, the Department further needs
to strengthen its spaceport infrastructure to meet the launch vehicle requirements. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the Department should increase its production capabilities so as to make the launch
vehicles ready in larger number and capture the global market. (Para 8.3)

5
Action Taken
In view of the launch demand for national/user specific requirements along with the possibility of
increasing the commercial footprint in the global market, the Department has been making focused
efforts to increase the throughput of systems and stages for the launch vehicles from the industry and
increase the frequency of launches in a year. The annual launch frequency is steadily increasing and has
increased from 2-3 launches during the initial period of the 12th Five Year Plan to 6 launches by the end
of the Plan period. In the case of PSLV, during the 12th Five Year Plan period, 19 Missions have been
achieved against the projected target of 17 Missions. Considerable reduction in average launch campaign
duration has been achieved, which has also contributed to the increase in the launch frequency. Additional
industry participation is being identified/qualified and the capacity at the existing work centres is also
being augmented to further increase the PSLV launch frequency to eight per year. Department is also
planning to enhance the capacity within the country to produce operational flights of PSLVs through a
Joint Venture with Indian Industries. This will make available more vehicles as well as spare capacity
to establish a stronger presence in the global market.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department and would like to be apprised of the
roadmap prepared by Department to enhance the capacity within the country to produce operational
flights of PSLVs through a Joint Venture with Indian Industries.
SPACE SCIENCES & PLANETARY EXPLORATION:
Recommendation
The Committee appreciates the achievements of the Department with regard to its Space Sciences
& Planetary Exploration programme during the 12th Plan period. The Committee hopes that the target
of the Department for launching Chandrayaan-2 mission in 2017-18 will be realised within the fixed
time. (Para 9.3)
Action Taken
CHANDRAYAAN-2, the second Indian Lunar mission, comprises of indigenous Lander, Rover and
Orbiter modules. The Orbiter development is progressing well with various subsystems of the module
in advanced phase of testing. Demonstration models of the indigenous Lander have been completed.
Mechanism elements of the Rover module are nearing completion. The Department is working towards
the launch of Chandrayaan-2 as per the targeted schedule in 2017-18.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department.
Recommendation
The Committee further observes that the Aditya-L1 mission of the Department which was initially
set to be realised during the 12th Five Year Plan has not been realised till date. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the Department should speed up the launch of Aditya-L1 mission within a
fixed time frame. (Para 9.4)

6
Action Taken
Aditya mission was envisaged to realise a polar orbiting satellite with Solar Coronagraph as its sole
payload to study the solar corona. With the recent understanding of solar exploratory missions, the scope
of Aditya mission have been expanded and renamed as Aditya - L1. The spacecraft is now mooted to
be placed in an orbit about 1.5 million kilometers from the Earth (three times farther than the moon)
known as the Lagrange point or the L1 point to ensure continuous observation of the Sun. Besides the
Solar Coronagraph, the mission will now carry 6 more scientific instruments on-board for observation
of solar corona, photo-sphere, chromo-sphere and solar wind. With its revised scope the launch of the
mission is now targeted in 2019-2020. (Para 9.4)
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department.
CAPACITY BUILD-UP
Recommendation
The Committee is not satisfied with the progress achieved by the Department during the 12th Five
Year Plan on account of capacity build-up. The Committee notes that the Department envisioned
establishment of Third Launch Pad at Sriharikota to support the increased launch frequency of PSLV
and GSLV during the 12th Plan period whereas no budgetary support has been sought by the Department
for the purpose during the years 2015-16 and 2016-17. The Committee fails to understand as to why
the Department did not seek any budgetary support for the purpose. The Committee strongly feels that
the Department has failed to lay due focus on the establishment of Third Launch Pad. The Committee,
therefore, recommends the Department to furnish the reasons for being so tardy on this count.
(Para 10.3)
Action Taken
With regard to the observation of the Committee on account of unsatisfactory progress on
establishment of Third Launch Pad at Sriharikota, the following points are brought to the notice of the
Committee:
• The Department had envisioned establishment of Third Launch Pad during 12th Plan period
to support the increased launch frequency of PSLV and GSLV . The Department had identified
the site and initiated action on preparation of the project report for the facility. However, due
to the two successive failures of two GSLV flights during 2010, the Department had to focus
on tiding over the technological bottlenecks related to cryogenic technology.
• The Department has now overcome the technological issues and has established GSLV as a
reliable launch vehicle for launching 2 Tonne class of satellites into Geo-synchronous Transfer
Orbit.
• During this period, the Department has worked around the existing two launch pads to support
the requirements by resorting to a series of measures like, (i) reducing the PSLV launch

7
campaign duration; (ii) reducing launch pad refurbishment time required between launches and
(iii) augmenting the second Launch Pad with Subsystem Assembly Building enabling simultaneous
integration of two vehicles.
• The Department has also taken up establishment of a Second Vehicle Assembly Building with
a total approved amount of ` 629.12 crore. The work on the facility is progressing well and
is expected to be ready by the end of 2017-18.
• With the above measures, the overall launch capacity is expected to increase to 12-14 launches
per year as compared to the current capacity of 8 launches per year.
• The Department will initiate action on setting up the Third Launch Pad, including obtaining
necessary approvals, once the enhanced capacity becomes fully operational.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department and would like to be further informed
of the progress achieved in the matter.
Recommendation
The Committee notes that the Department has failed to furnish any information about the progress
achieved on account of setting up of Space Technology Parks at different locations to facilitate industry
participation in Indian Space Programme. The Committee would like to be informed of the progress
achieved in the matter. (Para 10.4)
Action Taken
During 12th Five Year Plan period, in order to enhance the participation of Indian industry in Space
programme, vendor complexes are built at various Centres/Units where qualified vendors realise different
subsystems/modules of space systems. This has provided the basic infrastructure built-up for the partner
industries to realise various hardware systems/sub-systems for the Indian space programme. Assembly,
Integration and Testing activities of two navigation satellites have been outsourced to a consortium of
Indian industries. Similarly, an outreach facility has been established at NRSC, Hyderabad to enable
vendors to participate in Indian Space Programme.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department.

Recommendation

also notes that the Department did not seek either any budgetary support or very negligible support for
its crucial programmes such as Cryogenic Upper Stage Project (CUSP); Semi-cryogenic Engine Clustering;
Semi-Cryogenic Stage Development; Advanced Launch Vehicle Development; Resourcesat-3 & 3A; Solid

Launch Pad and Space Capsule Recovery Experiment (SRE-I&II) during the year 2015-16 and 2016-

(Para 12.5)
Action Taken
With regard to the observations of the Committee for not allocating funds for the above mentioned
schemes/projects/programmes during 2015-16 and 2016-17, the following points are brought to the
notice of the Committee:
• With the launch of four successful flight of GSLV with indigenous cryogenic stage, the overall
objectives of Cryogenic Upper Stage Project (CUSP) have been achieved. The Project has
been formally closed. Hence, separate budget was not sought.
• The objectives of Space Capsule Recovery Experiment has been achieved with the successful
launch and recovery of Crew Module Atmospheric Re-entry Experiment (CARE) during
December 2014 with this, the project has been formally closed. Hence, no projections were
made.
• While the Department has established Cryogenic technology with four successful launches of
GSLV , the work towards development of next generation Semi-cryogenic Engine is progressing
well and is expected to be ready by 2020-21. Based on the progress made so far on development
of the engine, activities towards Semi-cryogenic Stage Development is proposed to be taken

are presently in discussion stage for arriving at suitable configurations. Once the detailed

9
project reports are finalized, the Department will take necessary approvals towards these
activities and suitable budget provisions will be made.

during the fag end of 2016-17. Hence, no cash-flow was envisaged during 2015-16 &
2016-17. Towards realisation of these programmes, the Department has made provisions in
BE 2017-18.

Recommendation
The Committee appreciates the activities undertaken by the Centre for the overall growth of our
North Eastern Region (NER) with the help of its expertise in space technologies. The Committee during
its study visit to NE-SAC observed that space technologies could be used in tackling vector borne
diseases like dengue and Chikungunya by right kind of advices to the locals for better protection. The
Committee, therefore, feels that in order to bring better awareness on even disease warning etc.,
NE-SAC can play an important role by effective use of its satellite based communication network.
(Para 18.8)
Action Taken
North Eastern Space Applications Centre (NESAC), Shillong in collaboration with Regional Medical
Research Centre (ICMR), Dibrugarh developed an early warning system for Japanese Encephalitis (JE)
disease for the endemic districts of Assam following an integrated approach using geospatial techniques,
meteorological data and data on disease epidemiology. The project, started in 2003, was validated for 5
years during the period 2008-2012 and now operationalised in three most JE prone districts in Assam,
viz., Dibrugarh, Tinsukia and Sivasagar. The project is now included as Programme of Translational
Research by ICMR and every year forecasting is issued to the concerned health authorities on disease
onset, disease intensity and disease prone villages of JE.
A user friendly open source GIS based software package named Japanese Encephalitis Early
Warning System (JEWS) has been developed for use of the concerned health authorities. The software
package has been formally handed over to the concerned health authorities in Assam during a workshop
organised in Guwahati, Assam in August 2014. Based on the forecast generated with the JEWS, Regional
Medical Research Centre (ICMR) issues advisories to the State Health department for taking various
control measures such as spraying of DDT, distribution of impregnated mosquito net, vaccination etc.

17
Under a EOAM funded project, NESAC has created digital database on six most important vector
borne diseases of NER viz., Malaria, JE, Chikungunya, Dengue, Filariasis and West Nine virus for all
the states of the region. Spatial and temporal distribution of disease cases has been mapped and disease
occurrence hotspots have been identified for suggesting intervention measures. Based on suggestions
given by the Honourable Parliamentarians, NESAC is planning to work towards developing early warning
system for diseases like Chikungunya and Dengue on a pilot mode in collaboration with ICMR and state
health departments.
